The Master said, "Reverend, at this very moment, in which position do you stand? The monk bowed. Small Assembly Instruction:
As the year’s end gives way to spring, every thing is wondrous; The ocean wind stirs the azure glass. Last night, by chance, I attained...
A Letter from Home: In a ruined monastery and desolate village, there is nothing left to rely upon.
Brothers, as for this home of Boshan—is it a ruined monastery? Is it a desolate village? If anyone can discern this, Boshan will join hands with them and return together.
If not, then for now let me add a speck of dust to the Lotus Sutra; another year has passed since the end of the Jambudvīpa cycle.
Small Assembly. After the monks had finished their questions, the Master said: "The age is called the five turbidities; the world is known as Saha.
The ground is a wasteland of mounds and ruins; the human heart is a thicket of briars. Green forests harbor poisonous vapors within one's palm; flies swarm upon the back of a broken donkey.

One practices by treading through fire and water, yet breathes out only the stench of raw meat and fat. Within the breast, there is not even a trace of Zen spirit, yet one forcibly fashions sharp mental flashes from the belly."

Within the bosom lies a single mass of filth. To stretch out and engage in question and answer, ghosts see it and clap their hands in laughter; when people encounter it, they turn their eyes askance in anger. One buries one's own spirit and brings shame upon the former sages.
Wash the heart and reform one's errors; do not pursue delusive conditions. If one does not repent past transgressions, the fruit will surely fall from the cause.
Have you not seen? At the assembly on Vulture Peak, those who truly understand were few; in the garden of the Elder, [the same was true].
"There are many wood-ear mushrooms. [The Master] struck his staff and descended from the seat.

At the informal sermon for the Shengsheng Society: "Matters within the School of the Patriarchs are difficult to express in words; they are those phrases that cannot be conveyed even by exerting one's full strength."
How can you open your mouth? Someone has already spoken regarding the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
Someone has already spoken regarding "this very mind is Buddha. Someone has already spoken regarding "neither mind nor Buddha.
Someone has also spoken regarding "not mind, not Buddha, not a thing. Now tell me, how will you distinguish these for your fellow practitioners?
"What must one analyze to attain it? After a long silence, he said: "Gold has its own price;
who would be willing to sell it mixed with sand? Be careful."
A Small Sermon at the Moonrise Hermitage. National Teacher Zhong said: "The green creeper winds its way straight up to the crest of the cold pine;
the white clouds drift indistinctly, appearing and disappearing within the great void. All phenomena are fundamentally tranquil, yet it is people who create their own clamor.

Brothers, right now—these mountains, rivers, and the great earth; the myriad phenomena in their dense array; the waterfowl and the trees; the crowds of people and the trampling of horses—what do you call this?
Regarding the myriad dharmas: how can one explain the principle of original stillness? To abandon the myriad dharmas in search of original stillness has never been possible.
To seek original stillness within the myriad dharmas requires that it burst forth from beneath the seam of one’s robes; only then is it attained.
Therefore, Boshan instructed people to take a single phrase of the *huatou* and place it within the field of the eighth consciousness, right between the eyebrows and the...
The earth is firmly bound; it only requires that you awaken to it yourself and accept it yourself. If this is not yet so, listen to this verse: Upon what do the Buddhas rely for their dwelling?
The meaning of the question at Vulture Peak is fresh. The Heart-essence serves as the head of the community;

Jin-sul acts as the patron. A single rain nourishes the land of spring; A thousand lamps thin the evening clouds. You must know that within the realm of dust, the ultimate and the conventional cannot be divided. Be careful! Be careful!
Invitation for the Small Assembly at Fushan Huayan Temple upon the Appointment of a New Abbot. The Great Perfect Enlightenment is our monastery;
furthermore, one should know that our monastery is the Great Perfect Enlightenment. They encompass and merge with one another, being non-dual and without distinction.

Only then can one respond to affairs and engage with others without any initial obstruction. Now, one who is well-established in upholding [the Dharma] first attains the fundamental immovable wisdom, and only thereafter attains the wisdom of differentiation.
Within the fundamental immovable wisdom, there is no room for even a hair’s breadth of discursive thought.

As for the wisdom of differentiation, it accords perfectly with every situation when responding to affairs and engaging with others; yet, if there is even a hair’s breadth of intentional deliberation, [it fails].
It is movable; as long as it has not yet escaped the characteristics of arising and ceasing, coming and going, it cannot be called wisdom.

One who attains this wisdom applies principle to phenomena, such that every phenomenon is entirely principle. If it were otherwise, it could not be called "abiding and maintaining. [The Master] did not see [the monk].
A monk asked, "What is it like when Yunmen does not give rise to a single thought? Yunmen said, "Mount Sumeru. Tiantong’s verse says: "Not giving rise to a single..."
Contemplate Mount Sumeru. Yunmen’s Dharma-giving is likewise not stingy; if you are willing to come, he hands it over with both hands.
If you intend to go, its ten-thousand-fathom height cannot be grasped. Mountains and seas are vast, white clouds are idle—do not allow even a hair’s breadth of attachment between them.
The crowing of a borrowed rooster cannot deceive me; I am unwilling to let anyone pass the barrier in a state of vagueness. Great Master Tiantong strikes the watch-sticks at the double gate.
To wait for violent guests, the keys and locks are held in one's own hands; the defense is most rigorous.
Formerly, the abbot of this mountain, Master Yuanlu, was a matchless player at chess—truly one who seizes the corners and breaks through the gates. Yet today, Bozan wishes to ask him:
before black and white have even been distinguished, how does one ultimately make this first move? From time immemorial, it has been the board of nineteen paths.
"How many are there who are deluded or awakened? Tell me, what is it they are deluded about? What is it they are awakened to? After a long silence, he said: "Take care!
This is the informal sermon at Zhongfang Temple on Mount Dàlóng. If one wishes to preach the Dharma, there is no dharma to be preached; there is nothing that can be preached."
This is what is called "preaching the Dharma. If there were a dharma that could be preached, it would surely bring disgrace upon the Great Dharma.
Long ago, when the World-Honored One ascended the seat, Mañjuśrī struck the mallet and said: "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma-King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma-King.

Thereupon, the World-Honored One descended from the seat. Brothers, tell me: did the World-Honored One have a dharma to preach, or was there no dharma he could preach? You people must look into this matter.
Only when one opens their inner eyes can this be understood. When Mañjuśrī spoke thus, where was he?
He saw the World-Honored One preaching the Dharma, and the World-Honored One immediately descended from his seat. Was this an approval of Mañjuśrī, or a disapproval of Mañjuśrī?
Brothers, can you discern this? If you have not yet realized it, listen to this verse: At the summit of White Cloud Mountain lies Fangzhong Monastery; its pure chanting is without end.
The assembly has settled and is at leisure; I only fear that the stream is deep and the current swift, lest there be too much falling of flower-rain upon the human world.
At the request of the Palace Counselor, Layman Wu Guanwo, this informal discourse (xiaocan) is given.

If you wish to investigate the matters of the Chan school, you must have correct faith in cause and effect, become thoroughly proficient in the teachings of the scriptures, contemplate the sufferings of the hells, and resolve to attain Bodhicitta. As an ancient worthy said: "Chan and Vinaya go hand in hand..."
They proceed without mutual obstruction or hindrance. If one discusses the pure and white ground of the mind, every person is fully endowed with it.

It is only because of the false arousal of a single thought that greed, anger, and ignorance arise. With the causes of greed, anger, and ignorance, one then experiences the effects of the three evil realms.
As the teachings state: "If one indulges in greed, there is the mechanism for an unceasing hell; if one suppresses oneself into anger, there is the limb [of existence] as a hungry ghost."
The suffering of being burned by fire is joined with delusion (*moha*). Within the realm of animals, they think only of water and grass, knowing nothing else.
If there were no greed, anger, and delusion, how could the three evil paths exist?

This is why Boshan instructs those in the various ranks to give rise to a single thought upon the pure and white ground, to single-mindedly uphold it with a resolute heart, so that when the final breath does not come, one will ultimately [attain liberation].
"Where has it gone? By all means, do not engage in conceptualization or measurement. To engage in conceptualization and measurement is called a 'medicinal taboo.
Master Yunqi said: 'The milk of a lion will crack a lapis lazuli vessel if it is poured into one;
the unsurpassed, wondrous Way cannot be contained by anything that is not a vessel of pure Dharma. Master Shaokang said: 'The supreme flavor of clarified butter emerges...'"
It is like adding a drop of water to milk; the two cannot coexist. What is called "a drop of water" refers precisely to the measuring of discursive thought (*vitarka-vicāra*).

If one is without such discursive measurement, one can enter directly with a single blade and forcefully break through the heavy encirclement. This is like the Grand Historian of Wu, who gave rise to the Mahāyāna mind and received the Mahāyāna precepts;
he was truly what is called a vessel for the pure Dharma. However, it was not yet known that there was a stage above this.

Matters. Today, the conditions have converged; strive to give rise to faith and aspiration. A verse says: "A lay practitioner resides north of the river, To whom devas and humans look up with reverence.

It is heard that the Golden Grain (Śākyamuni) has arrived; The circumstances of this encounter are remarkably similar. In discussing the mind, the autumn moon is bright; In expounding the teachings, the spring clouds arise.
As our spiritual resonance corresponds, I have been specially sent here. Strive to investigate the matter beyond the ordinary— How profound is that which transcends!"
The Essential Point. When kicking through one’s own toe, Master Wu of Shuzhou held a small *paramārtha* (small-scale teaching) at Pini Hermitage on Mount Hongtao:
"Fellow practitioners, when born you do not know whence you come; you cannot help but doubt the place from which you came. When dying you do not know whither you go;
you cannot help but doubt the place to which you will go. How could a true man of great character ever be willing to accept [this ignorance]?"
The mind receives retribution according to its karma. If one wishes to bring this matter to ultimate completion, it depends upon a single thought-moment of pure sincerity;
one must not be careless. As Xianglin took forty years before he finally achieved "one piece," and Lingyun required thirty years before he attained awakening upon seeing peach blossoms.
Therefore, Boshan taught people to contemplate a single phrase: "When the single breath does not come again, what then? Ultimately...
Where do you go? Whether walking or sitting, whether dressing or eating—when, in the end, this single breath does not return, where will you go?
Be careful not to engage in thought or discrimination; such thought and discrimination are utterly inconsistent with resolving this matter.
If you can truly investigate and earnestly examine it, one day while washing your face, you will touch your own nostrils.
Yet, this is still too close.

A small discourse: The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates and immeasurable wondrous meanings are entirely within the mind, intellect, and consciousness of all people; they are fully present therein.
If you identify with the mind, intellect, and consciousness, you will obscure the hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates. If you instead seek to realize them...
One attains hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates. Where does mind, intellect, and consciousness come from? A mere slight opening of a vital point can both kill a person and bring them to life.
All you practitioners of Chan should each open your eyes beneath the seam of your robes and devote this entire life to it.
To settle this matter, here is a small discourse.
Changqing said: "Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. Only when one consents of one's own accord does one become intimate with it.

Right now, the mountains, rivers, the great earth, the pavilions, terraces, ponds, and galleries—all these vivid greens and yellows before our eyes—are the myriad phenomena. What do you call that which reveals itself?
This body, revealed in its solitude. [The Master] holds up his staff and says: "Do not merely seek the beauty of the mountain scenery;
you must know that there is another spring in one's own old garden. He strikes the ground once with the staff.
A Minor Sermon for the Spirit of Layman Liu Hehe. Are you alive, sir? Or are you dead? Who says that empty space undergoes change?
Are you dead, sir? Or are you alive? Who says that the vast ocean can be overturned? Your life and death are perfectly clear;
though the winds of kalpas blow, they cannot stir you. Your wisdom-light is perfectly round; even if the fires of kalpas blaze, they cannot move it.
As for the Master’s inclinations, the fleshly eye cannot perceive them; as for his deeds and practices, who would not marvel at their excellence?
As for his realization, no one can equal its depth; as for his spiritual enjoyment, only the sages know it. The mountain colors of Xiafang remain empty through time and eternity;
listen silently as the dark-voiced monkeys cry out throughout the night.
Because of certain business, I have come late for the evening session. Tonight there is a fine moon; does the assembly see it? It may be said:

"The brilliance of the jade mirror pervades every place, yet how many are blind and their heads shrouded in darkness! Alas, those who do not accept the golden scalpel will remain white-headed until they finally pass away in the dark.
There have been no few commentators on this moon from ancient times to the present, from the time of the World-Honored One down to this very day.

From the thousands of worthies to the myriad sages, there is none who has not exerted their full strength to guide and uplift others. Their compassionate hearts are as urgent as those of an old woman;
yet, when examined closely, they can only speak of matters concerning the reflection of the moon. If you wish to see the true moon, you must open your own eyes.
What is called "the talk at Vulture Peak" or "Caoxi," or "Zhaozhou pointing south" or "playing with Hanshan"—these are merely descriptions that are vaguely similar and faintly resembling the reality.
"Rarely! Even if one could speak with tenfold perfection, Bozan would still not dare grant approval. Why? Because the divine talisman is not present behind the elbow;
everything remains within the pit of right and wrong. You all must exert yourselves to leap out of this barrier of right and wrong."
If you do not leap out of the pass of right and wrong, how will you withstand the darkness of the three realms? Take heed!

Compiled by the Dharma-grandson of Boshan, Honghan,
and the Head Seat Dharma-grandson, Hongyu, together with their assembly for a tea discourse.

An invitation for tea and conversation at the Three-Fathom Hall of the Heavenly Realm. Regarding the matters within the sphere of study and practice: one must immediately cause all people to comprehend them;
one must immediately be free from affairs. To do otherwise would already be to bury all people. Within this, there are three divergent paths.
There is a type of student who carries a Buddha about on their shoulders as they wander from house to house, even seeking out Buddhas and seeking out the Dharma. Seeking...
To seek the Way through meditation, or to seek the profound and the subtle, is to carry a burden wherever one goes; yet one's entire being is already the Buddha-dharma.
It is like a tortoise bearing a map—this is the very omen of its own destruction. It is like a phoenix entangled in a golden net—how can it ever expect to soar into the mists of heaven?
Furthermore, there is a type of practitioner who assumes mastery over themselves, claiming that there is no Buddha to be sought, no Chan to be investigated, and no Way to be studied.

They believe that by merely stripping away everything until it is pure and without dependence, this state is their own personal enjoyment. In reality, they have not yet reached the stage of true purity;
all such views arise from the mind of karmic consciousness. Even if such people with false views were to reach a state of purity, it would still be so.

"Brothers, it has never been permitted that there is any room for 'studying the Way' within these states. If one gives rise to the worldly offenses of greed, anger, and delusion, though they are grave, they are still light.
But to take a state of pure cleanliness and call it the ultimate limit of studying the Way—this karma is the most heavy;
there is nothing in the world equal to it. Brothers, you must simply overturn these two kinds of false views. Now tell me, toward what [should you turn]?"
Where can one find peace and happiness? An ancient worthy said: "What is the head? You must first know that it exists.
If you truly know that it exists, you need not worry about failing to exhaust the present moment.

The patriarchs of old have taken this single matter as the most wondrous and profound, like the taste of the *trivṛt* herb or the touch of a vajra-pestle. Only if you open your eyes here can you be permitted to speak.
A brief aside: Tonight, amidst the tea ceremony for the three abbots, I shall reveal a certain message. How will you all understand it?
If you can penetrate through these words, it will not be difficult; if not, it would be best for each of you to drink your tea and return to the hall.
At the request of the Minister of Rites, Layman He Zhiyue, a tea talk was held. Layman He asked, "An ancient worthy said: 'If you consent, you will forever be liberated from the roots and dust;
if you do not consent, you will forever sink into birth and death. As for this 'consenting' and 'not consenting,' one must wipe them both away at once.
May I ask, how does one enter? The Master raised his cup and said, "Please have some tea first. After a long silence, the Master asked, "Do you understand? The layman replied, "Yes."
A brief summary. The Master said: "By no means should you linger here. He then said: "Few know the matter of the ancestral gate;
the great causal conditions each have their own time. Today I shall open a single thread for you: the clear breeze and bright moon fill the stream before us."
At the request of Layman Pan Cilu, I offer these words of tea-talk at Daruo Hermitage: The clouds atop Mount Touzi shift and transform throughout all time.
Only after crossing Zhaozhou’s Bridge does one finally transcend thought and calculation. To say that transcending thought and calculation is only half the journey is incomplete;
there remains another half. As the text continues below, I shall leave it for tomorrow morning. Take care.

After the snowfall, I took several Zen practitioners to the Nanlai Pavilion for tea and conversation. On this day when great snow sealed the mountains, we met by chance atop the tiered tower in joyful accord.
The cold was so intense that the crows remained silent; the white frost bound the mists into masses. The Zen mind is pure and still; the realm of form is cool and vast.
Knowing clearly that it is all water, do not let yourself be deceived by it.
At the request of the Chan practitioners of Wufangzhushan, this informal talk on tea: Do you wish to know where Boshan’s practice lies?
At the fifth watch of the night, incense is burned; at dawn, there is early morning gruel; at noon, the midday meal.
When walking, I walk together with you all; when sitting, I sit together with you all. When drinking tea, I drink tea with you all; when conversing, I converse with you all. Only...
There are certain points where we differ; I cannot help but speak of them to the great assembly.
You all engage in deliberation, whereas Bo Shan has no deliberation. You all seek the Buddha-dharma, whereas Bo Shan has no Buddha-dharma to be sought.
You all see Bo Shan and all external objects, yet Bo Shan does not see you, nor does he see any objects outside of the mind. And now...
There are only a few ribs and two pieces of skin; he is just like everyone else. The verse says: Welcoming guests and attending to visitors is an ordinary matter;
He cannot even speak of the wondrous or discourse on the profound. Of what use is this master?
How dare he leave his name behind to be transmitted in the Lamp Records?
Invited by Layman Zhuo Wuliang for a tea talk: To study Chan is to resolve the matter of life and death; to recite the Buddha's name is likewise to resolve the matter of life and death.
Nowadays, people suppress the Pure Land and propagate the principles of Chan. From the perspective of the ancients, it would have been acceptable to lead people to enter deeply through a single gate.
To distinguish between superior and inferior is merely the business of you all. To recognize the mind and yet rely on others to form interpretations—how could this possibly...?
However, they do not understand the principles of Chan, nor have they even dreamt of the single gate of Pure Land.
My late master Yunqi bound these two paths—Chan and Pure Land—together into one bundle, teaching people to single-mindedly hold up the phrase: "Who is it that recites the Buddha's name?
That this word "who" remains uncomprehended is evident here in the "blow-off-sheath sword" and the "poison-coated drum. This word "who" remains uncomprehended.
There is no need to look back or forward; you must simply exert yourself and suddenly give rise to the great doubt-mass.
Whether it be Chan or Pure Land, what does it matter? It is like a single person facing ten thousand enemies: until this mass of doubt is shattered, do not vow to rest.
Only those who are truly men of great strength can understand this. Otherwise, you will fall into the mud or the water, caught between being and non-being, regarding birth and death.
At the gateway, there is no point of contact whatsoever. A capable student takes that single word "Who" which remains unclarified;
with their eyebrows joined to the great earth, they form a single mass. Standing amidst a thousand or ten thousand people, they do not see a single person.
Heaven and earth revolve, mountains and rivers run; waves overturn and billows surge. Unknowingly and unawares, one’s entire being is within the cave of principle.
It is as if sitting amidst a silver mountain and an iron wall—one simply must burst open a single thread.
This single thread is the path that ascends upward; it is the matter not transmitted by the thousand sages. If you can realize this matter, then you may proceed toward Vairocana.

To perform a somersault atop the crown of Lu Ding’s head would not even be considered extraordinary. To speak of "transcending the four propositions" and "cutting off the hundred negations" is all superfluous talk.
If it were not like this—how could one truly identify a person who recites the Buddha's name and take up this matter? It would be nothing short of a grievous error.
This is like mistaking a donkey’s saddle bridge for one’s father’s chin—it is enough to provoke a laugh. Truly, such a person is of a volatile temperament;

as soon as they hear the word "Who," it is as if they were wielding the Vajra King’s precious sword, forcefully breaking through heavy encirclements and reducing the great earth to a hundred fragments.
They cast the word "Who" away into the worlds of other directions without even needing to lift it up—act as one such!
This solitary, towering, and majestic fellow may speak of Chan; he may also speak of the Pure Land.
He may speak in a manner that matches shoulder-to-shoulder and hand-to-hand with the Tathāgata; yet he may also leave not even a single character for "Buddha" behind. Why is this?
If one were to use the word "Buddha" to further define the Buddha, one would betray the heart of the ancient Buddhas of yore. Be careful! Be careful!

Tea Talk: The hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates all dwell within the square inch of the heart-mind; the wondrous virtues as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are all contained within the source of the mind.
All gates of precept, concentration, and wisdom are fully possessed therein; all supernatural powers and sublime functions are fully possessed therein;

the four fruits and four stages of realization are fully possessed therein; the twelve links of dependent origination, in their forward flow and reverse cessation, are fully possessed therein; and the five faculties...
The five powers, up to and including the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment that serve as the causal conditions for the path, are all spontaneously complete within him.
The six perfections and the myriad practices are all spontaneously complete within him. The ten powers and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha are all spontaneously complete within him.

The three stages of worthiness and the ten stages of sagehood are all spontaneously complete within him, even unto the ultimate fruit of Buddhahood, which is all spontaneously complete within him. He descends from the royal palace and emerges from his mother’s womb. Up to...

On the Snowy Mountains, he practiced asceticism; beholding the morning star, he opened the Eye of the Path; and so on, until he preached the Dharma to benefit sentient beings—all these were spontaneously and fully accomplished by himself.
Brothers, since everything was spontaneously and fully accomplished, why is there a missing corner in the southeast of the Buddha Hall?

Listen! Attend! At the request of the lay practitioner Li Taichong, this informal discourse on tea is given. Afflictive conditions are easily encountered, yet the work of the Way is difficult to accomplish.
If you do not resolve the myriad distinctions of present circumstances, how will you deal with all external conditions? How will you deal with the mountains, rivers, and the great earth?
How do the grasses, trees, and forests come to an end? How do the myriad phenomena of the forested universe come to an end? How do human tracks and bird footprints come to an end?
How do the four great elements and the five aggregates come to an end? How do the sense bases, objects, and consciousnesses come to an end?
Fundamental ignorance—how is it resolved? The flowing of the fetters—how is it resolved? Brothers, even if you understand, you are still wrapped within it;
even if you do not understand, you are still wrapped within it. Break through this wrapping directly!
Once you have broken through it directly, who is "I"? The pomegranate flowers outside the wall are not fire.
The World-Honored One universally taught by holding up a flower, and Kāśyapa smiled. Boshan once had a verse that said: "Auspicious petals and numinous branches, a spring beyond the kalpas;
held up, they stir the clouds over the seas and mountains. How much more so this compassionate heart, as vast as heaven—how could it be willing to drag through mud and mire?"
"Moving through the water. This verse was preserved by the World-Honored One for future generations; it possesses this segment of true wind.
To pick it up at hand when the occasion arises—at such a moment as this—to descend into the weeds to seek out a person, only Venerable Kāśyapa rose to the bait upon a single cast.
Transmitted from generation to generation down to the twenty-eighth patriarch, he came across the sea, not relying on written words, but pointing directly to the human mind to see one's nature.
He attained Buddhahood and received the "settling of the mind" from the Second Patriarch; he severed his arm until the blood flowed and reached the marrow.
The Third Patriarch repented his sins, and his madness was cured, becoming an exemplary model. Between the pestle and mortar, Layman Lu suddenly clarified the Great Dharma.

By polishing a brick to make a mirror, the "Colt" leapt forth from within the stables of Mount Nanyue. Holding his life-destiny, he sought and contemplated; amidst the mountains of Qingyuan, he looked upon it with a smile.

The rhinoceros horn is revealed—lofty and majestic. He has slipped free from the seal of Baizhang; he received three painful blows of the staff under Huangbo and was brought back to life beneath Huangbo’s walking stick.
He kicked over the pure water jar and went straight to Mount Daowei. Upon seeing his own reflection, he attained great enlightenment.
He composed the *Treasure Mirror Samādhi* with no lingering doubt. With his legs and shins snapped clean through, he entered directly into the Hall of the Patriarchs.
Aha! A single stone slab suddenly reveals the entire mechanism of the Dharma-eye.
From the Tang, Song, and Yuan dynasties down to our own dynasty, for over two hundred years, the lineage has continued unbroken until reaching my late Preceptor Shouchang.

He entered the gateway of Xingshan amidst the great, magnificent mountains; and Boshan followed in the fragrant dust of Chuanzi at a place where traces are hidden and no footprints remain. This matter—
Truly difficult; how could it be easy? It brings me back to the time when Boshan first resolved his mind [for enlightenment]. He followed the current downstream, traveling directly to the capital.
There, at Waguan Temple, beneath the seats of the Three Great Masters, he heard the *Lotus Sūtra* which says:

"Suppose there were a person who ascended to the summit of Mount Sumeru and proclaimed the twelve divisions of the scriptures for others—this would not be considered difficult. At that point, [the text continues:]
"After my parinirvāṇa, to even briefly read this sutra will be difficult. At that time, Boshan consulted various lecturers, asking:
"Is this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* outside of the twelve divisions of the scriptures? The lecturers replied:

"Even though it belongs to the Perfect and Sudden teaching (*yuan-dun jiao-men*), it is nonetheless subsumed under the Great Vaipulya (*dafangguang*). This was because those who propagate this Dharma after the Buddha’s passing [regarded it as such].
"This is indeed difficult. Boshan Qiansi said: "To seek it, one must look within oneself; how can one merely follow the words and chase the phrases?

He then went to visit Master Tong of Jing’an on Mount Wutai and received his instruction on the principle of the Three Contemplations (*sanguan*). First, he practiced the contemplation of emptiness (*śūnyatā-vipaśyanā*):
"When all is empty, everything is empty. At that moment, upon his meditation cushion, he suddenly became unaware of his physical body, blood, flesh, mind, or spirit.
Regarding the external realm: for five years he remained unaware of the existence of mountains, rivers, and the great earth.

While dwelling in seclusion atop the White Cloud Peak (Baiyunfeng) of Guanzhe, he met his senior dharma brother, Master Yinzong. Yinzong cited the verse: "Where the body is hidden, there are no traces; where there are no traces, do not hide the body.
He asked this of Boshan, who at that time answered as fluently as a flowing stream. Yinzong was also delighted. When the Master descended the mountain, he again brought [the matter] up...
Where the body is hidden, there is no trace; where there is no trace, do not hide the body. "I was at Yaoshan for over twenty years before I finally understood this kōan.
He repeated this several times. Unconsciously, it felt as if I were facing a wall of silver and iron.
Doubt suddenly arose, and I held it in mind day and night. Walking, I did not know I was walking; sitting, I did not know I was sitting; even with my clothes, I was unaware.
It was cold. He could not discern the flavor of his food; he would pluck vegetables without realizing there were vegetables, and pick tea leaves without realizing there were tea leaves.

When he set down his pack at a station, he would remain there for two hours before the pack grew heavy enough for him to move on again. He continued in this manner for a year and a half without any realization.
One day, while reading the *Chuan Deng Lu*, he came across Zhaozhou’s instruction to a monk: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell."
Where there was no Buddha, he hurried past in haste and immediately lost his cloth bag. Running on, he met Master Baofang;

during their exchange of questions and answers, it was like trying to fit a square block into a round hole. He remained there for two months, his face as yellow as paper and his skin barely covering his bones.
The Master took pity on him and cherished him. One day, when the Master accepted an invitation to Yushan Hermitage, he ordered an attendant to invite [the author] to join him.
We were traveling together. I said, "It is too hot; I will not go. My late teacher said, "There are people on the road who will preach the Buddha-dharma for you.
I replied, "Even if a living Buddha emits light, it is just a distraction. My late teacher called out to me repeatedly, and having no other choice, I traveled with him.
On the way, we discussed the principles of the Five Ranks of Sovereign and臣 (the subject). For the most part, he agreed with my views. As we were about to reach the foot of the hermitage, he asked:
I said: "The Great Master Foyin said, 'Ants know how to scurry toward where there is a stench; blue flies tend to fly toward where there is a foul odor.
This refers to the position of the ruler and the position of the minister. I said: "It is the matter of the minister's side.
My former teacher rebuked me, saying: "There are many who will laugh at you for this. I said: "Everything previously discussed was correct. Yet, why is it not so right here? My former teacher—

The Master said: "This one is not; all those are not. At Shang-an, while the former Master was seated with guests, I went to the rear garden and sat in *paryaṅka* (cross-legged) upon a flat rock for the duration of a meal.
Hearing the Dharma-protecting deity fall to the ground, my mind became transparently clear.
I immediately presented a verse to the former Master, which included the line: "With the single word of Yu-shan’s guidance, the heart is extinguished and the path of speech is cut off."
Regarding this phrase, my late teacher said, "Once you have entered one gate, you have entered many gates. I replied, "This is unnecessary.

Although my intellectual understanding was suddenly stilled upon reaching this point, alas, my mass of doubt remained unbroken. Consequently, I returned once more to the Zongmen Hall and stayed in seclusion for another half-year.
One day, while ascending the latrine, I saw a man climbing a tree; unconsciously, my body and mind leaped with joy, as if released.

Having laid down the thousand-pound burden, he took up his robes and departed. He traveled some fifty li into Baofang, yet he was unaware there was a road, nor did he perceive the movement of his own footsteps.
As soon as he entered the gate, he prostrated himself. The former master asked him:
"How have you been lately? I replied, "There is a living path, but it simply must not be known by others.
My late teacher asked, "Why must it not be known by others? I replied, "Not knowing, not knowing.

My late teacher said, "What kind of skillful hands and eyes does this old woman possess, that she burns the hermitage and drives the monk away? I replied, "It merely adds luster to the gold. My late teacher then raised [the case] once more.
A monk asked Chan Master Xuantze about the koan: "The dragon roars and mist rises; the tiger roars and wind is born. He commanded me to compose a verse on it. I took up my brush and wrote swiftly:
"Killing and enlivening vie for mastery, each possessing its own marvel; How could the dim-sighted perceive them? Though it emits light, it does not follow the whims of the age;
As before, the spring breeze pursues the horse's hooves. My late teacher smiled and said, "Today you have [attained it]."
"Only then did I believe that you were not deceiving me. I immediately asked, "Will there be anything further hereafter?
The former master said, "This old monk knows only the morning and evening meals; I do not know of anything further. I said, "Does the Master have no skillful means?
The former master said, "When you later attain the seat and don the robe, it will suffice if you are without any schemes. I—

He immediately prostrated himself. That winter, he presided over the assembly and presented me with a verse containing the lines: "The ultimate principles of the five schools are simultaneously threaded together;
the subtle essence of the Tripitaka is universally perfected. He further entrusted me, saying:

"You should maintain this through a continuous state of non-mind, correctly employing the practice of the exhausted Dharma to repay the compassionate grace that is beyond repayment, and to benefit those with right faith who possess the necessary conditions. O brothers, for this reason—

It was said: "This matter is truly difficult; how could it be easy? Today, because the Venerable Huitan from the Kingdom of Goryeo requested a general discourse, this Venerable One has traveled ten thousand *li* through treacherous and perilous terrain, braving the journey to have this Broad Mountain [monk] wag his tongue and move his lips to reveal the affairs of a lifetime.
As for the Great Master Śākyamuni and the Venerable Kāśyapa, let us set them aside for now."
Now tell me: when our late master Shouchang passed away, where has he gone now? Raising his whisk, he said:
"The light from the white tuft of hair illuminates the Palace of Ziwai; countless devas and humans weep like falling rain. Be careful."
Question and Answer:
A monk asked, "I do not ask about fragmented fragments or scattered remnants; please, Master, speak a single phrase of a brand-new decree.
The Master said, "Tearing asunder several layers of the pure world, riding a jade elephant backward to pursue the qilin. The monk pressed further, saying, "This is still merely..."
[The monk] presented a fragmentary scroll, whereupon the Master struck him. The monk said, "If so, then all under heaven is at peace, and the myriad people enjoy their vocations.
The Master said, "The mist of the South Mountain is sucked dry; the pines of the North Ridge endure forever. The monk bowed.
A monk asked, "The Great Master Jiashan said, 'To cut off the tongues of all people in the world is not impossible;
how can one teach a tongueless person to speak? I venture to ask the Master: what is the speech of a tongueless person? The Master raised his whisk and said:
"Do you understand? The student replied, "This is still the speech of one who has a tongue. Ultimately, what is the speech of one who has no tongue?
The Master said, "White clouds pervade the world; empty space neither comes nor goes. The student replied, "If so, then speech carries the profound yet leaves no path;
the tip of the tongue speaks, yet does not speak. The Master said, "Where did you see me, old monk?"
The monk stepped forward and said, "Only you, Reverend, could truly revitalize the Cao-Dong school. The Master said, "That too is merely idle talk. The monk bowed.
A monk asked, "An ancient said, 'There is a thing prior to heaven and earth. I do not know what this thing is.
The Master said, "Writing Sanskrit characters in the air. The monk pressed further, "Formless and fundamentally still and silent—is there still breath within the skull?"
The Master said, “Shattered to pieces, it does not form a pattern. The student asked, “It can act as the lord of the myriad phenomena; I wonder, are they the same or different?
The Master picked up his staff and said, “This cannot be called a ‘staff. The student asked, “It does not wither with the four seasons;
ultimately speaking, how far apart are they? The Master said, “Only then can this be called a ‘staff.’”
The student said, "At this very moment, throughout the world beneath heaven, fragrant oil continues the light of day and auspicious scenes manifest their grace.
What is the realm of Boshan? The Master said, "Moss coins are laid out upon the steps. The student said, "What is the person within the realm?
The Master said, "The bridge of the nose hangs downward."
A monk asked, "Śākyamuni Buddha preached the Dharma for forty-nine years; viewed with the correct eye, this was still like stirring up waves where there is no wind.
I venture to ask, Master: when you preach the Dharma, do you have any way of benefiting others?
The Master said, "It is a half-month's journey from here to Jiangxi. The monk pressed further, "If you were to encounter a person whose six sense faculties are incomplete, what would you do then?"
[The Master] said, "The waters of Bingxi are as clear as a mirror at the bottom. [The student] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this?
The Master said, "At the head of the Yangtze River, the waves splash to the heavens. [The student] said, "If that is so, then the Master’s kindness is great and difficult to repay.
The Master said, "After prostrating, withdraw."
The Layman Zhuo asked, "If all Buddha-lands are likewise empty, ultimately where does one go to adorn a pure land?
The Master said, "The deer are fat on Mount Qinglong. The Layman was speechless. The Master asked, "Do you understand? The Layman said, [I do]."
"No. The Master said, "Though the warbling orioles have their voices, no one hears the celestial music.
Layman Zhang Xinggong asked, "The Master says that a student must enter the principle with their whole being before they may inquire about matters above.
I now ask: what is this 'principle'? The Master said, "Lying across the body to face the universe; the great earth has no [separate] self."
[Zhalan] stepped forward and asked, "How can one immediately attain entry with the whole body? The Master said, "Exert all your strength to push your father toward the interior.
He [Zhalan] asked, "If one has not yet entered with the whole body, where does the fault lie? The Master said, "One treasures common pebbles while failing to distinguish the golden light.
He [Zhalan] asked, "When entering with the whole body, what serves as the verification? The Master said, "The ten directions vanish; one encounters [the Way] on both left and right."

Yuanjin asked, "After the whole body has entered the principle, what then? The Master said, "Only after leaping out of a thousand layers of waves can one boast of being a fish that has attained its heart's desire.
Chief Seat Six-Snows asked, "Learning relies on entering the room; knowledge leads to universal penetration. Setting aside 'entering the room' for a moment, as for 'universal penetration'—"
"How do you express this? The Master said, "The tethering rope has been cut, yet it can still be used.
He asked, "What is the matter of entering the room? The Master said, "A young child hammering a needle."
Question: "What is it like for one who sits and cuts off the realm of Vairocana’s enjoyment? The Master said: "Withered leaves piled in a heap. Question:
"Where does one who rides backward upon a lion tread? The Master said: "A goat’s gut and a bird’s path."
Question: "As for those who traverse the four seas sideways, I do not yet know what kind of skillful means they possess. The Master said: "A mere trifle. Question:
"As for those who let go their hands over a precipice, has the life-root still been severed? The Master said: "Wait until your own life-root is severed, and then I shall tell you."
Question: "How can the eight trigrams be arranged in their correct positions? The Master said: "One must not err in drawing a single stroke. Question:
"When encountering a fierce tiger on the road, how does one avoid it? The Master said: "Place your hands together at your chest."
Question: "Why were the iron trees and coral pierced by the mud ox? The Master said: "Who has witnessed this? Question:
"Who can pick up the stemless *dharma*-flower? The Master said: "The one without hands."
Question: "How can one draw water from the diamond-limit (vajra-sīmā)? The Master said: "Why such excessive effort? Question:
"In the Master's quarters, how many disciples are there? The Master said: "The character for 'heart' (心) with no dot added."
Question: "The patriarchs have transmitted robe and bowl to one another; I wonder, what do you, Master, transmit? The Master said:
"On the rock of the case-mountain, I shall deliberate with you."

Question: "Though one asks a thousand questions or ten thousand questions, they do not require so much as a single cough to be answered all at once. I wonder, Master, how do you answer such questions?
The Master said: "When you know the proper time, then withdraw."
A monk asked, "Last night I saw a reckless fellow who killed Vairocana Tathāgata. I wonder, how would one who understands the Dharma adjudicate this?
The Master said, "I would sentence him with full severity."
Question: What is the matter after the gavel has been struck? The Master said: "The waterfall has sound; the clouds do not conceal it. Question:
What is the matter before the gavel has been struck? The Master said: "The deep ravine has no fish; the water is naturally clear."
Question: "What is the matter of the 'striking the gavel'? The Master said: "Passing the morning with nothing to do; nodding the head in the dimming yellow light. Question:
"The ancients taught people until they reached the ultimate limit of the present moment. But once that limit has been reached, what then? The Master said:
Her hair was unkempt from neglect; she was glad to encounter a guest from the future.
He asked, "Within the gate of this pavilion, would you allow a man who has been dozing off to enter? The Master said, "I shall tell you once you have woken up."
Question: "Regarding Sudhana’s fifty-three pilgrimages, I wonder: does he still travel on foot today? The Master said:
"Wash your feet, get onto your bed, and sleep; in a single night, three thousand li."
Question: "Since Mount Laṅkā cannot be reached, why was it occupied by the Yakṣa King? The Master said: "The hand is close at hand;
the eye is swift. From head to foot, from bottom to top."
Question: When a turtle-nosed snake encounters a red-eyed person, how does one evade it? The Master said: "Just so, just so. Question:
One has clearly understood the essential tenets of the five houses; for what reason does the cycle of rebirth not cease? The Master said: "A weak fire burning the mountain."
"There is light, but no flame. Question:
The *Vimalakīrti Sūtra* says, "Remove all that exists, along with all attendants. Why does it say not to preserve even the attendants?
The Master said: "Long residence makes one despised; new arrivals speak with natural intimacy."
Question: "The World-Honored One opens his empty hands and clenches them; having clenched them, he opens them again. I do not yet understand what matter on that side he is clarifying.
The Master said: "I am only clarifying this very matter."
Question: "The ultimate firmness of all phenomena—does one not know that the Great Buddha-Crown is also contained within it? The Master said:
"In the dark, he draws out the transverse bone; in the light, he sits upon his own tongue."
Question: "The staff and the shout are like thunder; can they still provide offerings to the Bearded Yama? The Master said:
"If the Bearded Yama were to come, he too would have to eat the staff."
Question: "Does the skull of the former old monk still have eyes even now? The Master said: "An old crow in a cloth bag;
though alive, it is as if dead."
Question: Do Śākyamuni and Maitreya still respond to the two types of karma—projecting and completing? The Master said: "The two types of karma are the functional fruit of others;
what is there to say about responding or not responding?"

Question: The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* states that one "should give rise to a mind that dwells nowhere. Since there is nothing upon which to dwell, how then does one give rise to the mind?
Master: "Rock-flowers carpet the ground; a high autumn inspires the spirit. Pine-moon clasps the mountain; it announces the clarity of dawn."
A question was asked: "I do not like to hear the word 'Buddha. I do not seek to become a Buddha; how do you conduct your daily activities? The Master said:
"Swallowing food and gripping the chopsticks; lighting the fire and selecting dry wood."
Question: An ancient worthy said, "He has neither birth nor death. Why, then, are worldly people still driven by birth and death?
The Master said: "The green mountains have never moved; the bright sun deludes ghosts and men."
Midan Sheng asked about filial integrity and worthiness: "What kind of face is this? The Master said: "Heaven does not cover it; Earth does not support it. Midan Sheng pressed further:

"What is its ultimate realization? The Master said: "Earth does not support it; Heaven does not cover it. Midan Sheng asked: "By what means is it cultivated and realized? The Master said: [Heaven does not cover it; Earth does not support it.]
[The Master] was dressing, eating, attending to guests, and welcoming visitors.
A questioner asked: "What is the Sovereign? The Master said: "The waters of a clear pool are like ice. "What is the Minister? The Master said:

"Willow branches brush away the flying dust. "How does the Sovereign regard the Minister? The Master said: "An ancient mirror covered with white silk. "What is the Minister? The Master said: [He remains silent.]
[The Master] looked at the student. The Master said, "A slender hand presses down upon black clouds. [The student asked,] "What is the convergence of the Way between sovereign and subject?

The Master said, "One thread runs through it all. [The student] stepped forward and asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. [The student] asked, "What is this matter that lies beyond?
The Master said, "A tongue without bone; a wild horse without a halter."
Question: "What is the ruler? The Master said: "Water has sinews; mountains have bones. Question: "What is the minister? The Master said:
"The *jiji* bird cries as if weeping. Question: "What is the ruler looking at the minister? The Master said: "A thousand-year-old tree hangs with withered vines."

"What is it like for the minister to look upon the sovereign? The Master said, "The painted drum atop the tower strikes the third watch. "What is it like for the Way of Sovereign and Minister to be in harmony?
The Master said, "The golden palace gate: the phoenix carries off the vermilion edict; at the frontier, the people sing songs of victory as they return. The monk bowed.
The Master again asked the monk, "What is the matter within the position of the Sovereign? The monk said, "Vast and towering. The Master then struck him.
Question: "What is the realm of Boshan? The Master said: "Before the Phoenix-Perching Cliff, the clouds gather thick;
within the Dragon-Bathing Pool, the waves surge. Question: "Who is the person within the realm? The Master said: "Guang shaves his head;
Jing washes his bowl. The monk said: "I do not understand. The Master said: "This fellow has never yet shaved his head."
Question: "What is the Way? The Master said: "Red silk. The student asked: "Is red silk not the Way? The Master said: "It is not the Way. The student asked:
"If it is not the Way, why did you answer 'red silk'? The Master said: "Because you asked about the Way, I answered you with 'red silk.'"
Question: "Before Bodhidharma came to this land, did the Buddha-dharma exist or not? The Master said: "It existed. The questioner pressed:
"What is this future Buddha-dharma? The Master said: "Heaven cannot cover it; earth cannot carry it. The questioner pressed: "What kind of thing is so vast? The Master said:
"One must not call it a 'thing'. The questioner pressed: "When one does not call it a thing..."
"How is it? the Master said. "There is no place for you even to open your mouth. The monk stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then there is nothing to be done.
The Master said, "I, too, have nothing to do. The monk asked, "Why, Preceptor, do you have nothing to do?
The Master said, "Because you have nothing to do. The monk bowed. The Master said, "Go out! Even if you could save a thousand or ten thousand people, what would it avail?"

Question: "What is the place where such-and-such a person establishes their body and sustains their life? The Master said: "The sky has no cover; the earth has no bottom. The questioner pressed further:
"When the Elder Shouchang passed away, where is he now? The Master said: "In clear conversation, face to face."
"It is simply that you do not know. The monk asked again. The Master said, "Set aside your question for a moment. Heaven has no cover; earth has no bottom. Where lies the old monk’s intent?
As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. Yuanmian said, "When one presses out the marrow of space, it has flavor;
when one overturns the universe, there is no reliance. Within this, the Old Man Shouchang is not seen; there is only the cat."
He smiled and raised his eyebrows.
He asked, "What is it like to hide one's body within the Big Dipper? The Master said, "Turn yourself around. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him and further presented this verse:
"Turning yourself around to answer the Big Dipper— The phrase 'hiding the body' leaves no room for origin. If you wish..."
[Zhi Da] said, "The Great Elephant knows the road to Jiazhou; snow covers the deep mountains, all white-headed.
[The student] asked, "When cold and heat drive one another on, what then? The Master said, "The cauldron and the furnace coals.

[The student] further asked, "Before it has been processed, what then? The Master said, "A scene of shame upon the pure ground. [The student] further asked, "After it is completed, what then? The Master said, [silence].
Magnificent and exquisite—a scene of sheer embarrassment. A student asked, "What about matters at home? The Master said, "The one sitting sits."
The Master was lying down when the monk approached him and asked, "How are matters outside the gate? The Master said, "The countryside is treacherous; carts and horses find it difficult to pass.
The monk asked, "How are matters regarding people's affairs, Preceptor? The Master said, "I have never, from the beginning, wasted salt or sauce. The monk asked again.
"Where does one go when returning? What is the timing? The Master said, "I happen to be sitting or lying down right now.
The Master asked the Head Seat, Six-Snow: "The Head Seat of the Hall is the Eye of Humanity and Heaven. What is this 'Eye of Humanity and Heaven'? The Head Seat said, "On the crown of the head.
The Master said, "Is there still any need for reflection and discernment? The Head Seat said, "Do you not see it, Master? The Master [remained silent].
[The Master] said, "It is not in vain that you have come to meet a master. [Wuzhe] covered his ears and left.
The Master asked Senior Monk Wuzhe, "When you, my worthy brother, arrived at Luofu and intended to meet Boshan, what was it like?"
Zhai said, "The entire realm has never been hidden. The Master said, "If that is so, then you do not see me. Zhai said, "Two colors, one match.
The Master said, "You must still have a further direct encounter before you will succeed. Zhai said, "I have no second tongue. The Master said, "Wait until you reach Mount Luofu;
when you cannot move a single step in the pitch-black night, then you will truly penetrate deeply. The Master then gave him instruction.
A single verse: "Throughout the world, it has never been hidden. Green pines screen the azure cliffs; in the black night, footsteps find it hard to move; in the deep mountains, gods and ghosts weep.
Having selected this verse, the next day he entered the master’s presence and asked, "If one is a phoenix chick, one does not seek it elsewhere.
The Master said, "If one is a phoenix chick, then right here is fit to be marvelous. Zhe said, "This is the meaning of the saw. The Master—
Yunping stepped forward and bowed. The Master posed four questions:
"When the wind at the corner of the hall shakes the trees and all passersby take off their clothes, what is it like? Yunping replied, "In a mere flash, I have tasted it;
its coolness penetrates to my very marrow."

Question: "The clear breeze turns the white feathers; the village elder smiles in mutual intimacy. At such a time, what is it like? He replied: "When spring comes to the flower groves, the woodsmen and herdsmen harbor their emotions."
Question: Why is there a missing corner in the southeast of the Buddha Hall? He replied: "One person transmits a falsehood; ten thousand people transmit it as truth. Question:
How many people are sitting or lying in the Sangha Hall? He replied: "Turning over on the peak, six do not conspire together."
Chen Yunyi asked, "The thirsty deer chases a mirage; how can it be made to rest? The Master said, "If one knows it is not water, then it is finished.
He offered this verse: "From of old, the great earth has been dark and vast; Ultimately, what shall be used as a guide? If you recognize it, the waves are still."
Originally it was water; the present case is already established, so there is no need for investigation.
A questioner asked: "The mani jewel has long been buried in dust and soil; how can one urgently seek it out? The Master said: "What is the use of seeking it?"
The verse says: In every land and within every atom lies a priceless pearl; why needlessly create distinctions in vain?
One wears clothes and eats food, using it constantly; yet one lacks not a single point therein.
Question: "To cut through all at once—how does one obtain such a sharp sword? The Master said: "Tsk! Who dares face its edge? The Verse says:
Seeking it through many causes, you imagine it difficult to find; Never yet drawn from its scabbard, it makes the Ox and Cow constellations cold.
Its precious light shines brightly, illuminating heaven and earth; To wear it upon your person, why need you look upon it face-to-face?
Question: "The flavor of the water is the same throughout; yet there is one variety that constitutes the first spring and another variety that constitutes the second spring.
How is this distinction made? The Master said: "Only by tasting it can one know."
The verse says: When the fruit reaches the summit of the Golden Mountain, the stone walls beyond the city naturally diverge.
Having severed the crimson silken cord at one's heels, you should surely know the sacred source of the fragrant waters.
Question: "In the dead of night, one mistakes a thief for a son, or mistakes a son for a thief; how should this be judged? The Master said:
"If you call his name, he will respond. He spoke in verse: "There is no need to distinguish Chu from Qin; Who, right here and now, would be the second person? Take up that single blade well."
All are completely severed. Gold, brass, jade, and stone—all are family treasures.
A question was asked: "When one's own kin act as malevolent spirits, how should one deal with them? The Master said: "Slay them all; this is the summer retreat."
The verse says: With ash on the head and dust on the face, devoid of human sentiment; only when all are slain does one see true peace.
Within this, a single thread of sympathetic understanding runs through; when day breaks, as before, they remain pitiable creatures.
Question: "How can one truly behold the Master face-to-face? The Master said: "He who seeks to see him does not see him clearly.
The Verse says:
Fierce as a bear or a tiger, alive as a dragon— When has he ever been momentarily obscured from the Master? Furthermore, regarding this face-to-face encounter...
Seeking to meet you face-to-face, I know that green mountains lie between us—how many layers?
He asked: "The compass of the householder is capable of being moved in all directions, yet its needle always points south. Who is the master behind this? The Master said:
Truly, he has an iron heart and guts.

The verse says: Clearly manifest is an iron heart and guts; To turn back chaos and stabilize heaven and earth, nothing can hinder him. His loyalty and righteousness are pervasive as he serves the Sage Lord;
How could he be unwilling to let his name and lineage spread throughout all quarters?
Question: "A home is the livelihood for the bodies and lives of all people. What do you see that allows you to be willing to destroy your family and squander your property?
The Master said: "Only one who understands how to act as a master can."
The verse says: Having destroyed his home and squandered his wealth, he is utterly without reliance; yet he retains the radiant tuft of hair between his brows.
He does not seek a livelihood before others; with his head and horns extending freely, he manifests his full majesty.
Question: "A fine steed among lightning flashes covers a thousand li in an instant. How can one go after it and catch up, seizing the reins and bringing them into one's hand?
The Master said, "The reins are already in your hands, Layman; why would you need to pursue them?"

The verse says: A fine steed chases the wind, looking back at its shadow as it responds to the whip; yet for one who has forgotten conditions, the tether remains unloosed even before they have set out.
There is no need to grasp the reins and boast of one's diligence; beneath their feet, the black pearls are each perfectly round.
Question: "Great Wisdom, you say you have used a single blade to cut through the eight consciousnesses; upon what do you rely to establish yourself and find your livelihood?

The Master said: "Completely at ease. He spoke in verse: "A single stroke has truly struck down the chief culprit; How many times has he wandered upside-down throughout Jambudvīpa? Only when one recognizes Jing Mountain..."
In the place of kindness, the wooden man has no tongue, yet his speech is like thunder.
A question was asked: "Before a word is even spoken, why do you immediately strike and shout? The Master said: "The heart of a thief is always apprehensive."
The verse says: "The sphere of action of a Great Man is not ordinary; When apprehending a thief, one must verify the actual evidence.
It is not like those blind and sightless fellows of today, Who recklessly grasp their staffs to engage in idle deliberation."

Question: "When a Hu comes, a Hu appears; when a Han comes, a Han appears. Is this the substance of the mirror, or is it the light of the mirror? The Master said: "There is no room for anything to settle or cling;
its function is applied according to the occasion."
The verse says: Who argues over whether it comes from Hu or Han? Its brilliance illuminates heaven and mirrors earth—truly sublime!

It weighs seven *jin*.

Case: Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty asked Master Bodhidharma, "What is the primary meaning of the Noble Truths?

Case: The King of East India invited the twenty-seventh patriarch, Prajñātāra, for a vegetarian feast. The King asked, "Why do you not read the sutras?

The Master held up his whisk and said: "A needle at a perilous place, a wedge at a secure spot. The National Master probes the source; he wets what cannot be wetted and drives in a nail where none can enter.

Such is the venerable one’s skillful eloquence. Has the sutra been turned back yet? Wait until the thread beneath your heels is severed, and only then will you know how to believe, accept, and practice."

Case: One day, Nanyuan saw two halls disputing over a cat. Nanyuan held up the cat and said, "If you can speak, I will not kill it. The assembly had no response.

[Zhaozhou] picked it up and said, "A living capture, a live seizure. Old Wang’s total mastery; reviving the dead and returning life.

Case: On the road to Mount Tai, there was an old woman who, whenever a monk asked, "Where does the road to Mount Tai lead?", would say, "Go straight ahead.
As soon as the monk took a step, she would say, "What a fine master you are, yet you still go like that!
A monk reported this to Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou said, "I shall examine him for you. Zhaozhou then asked, "Where does the road to Mount Tai lead?"
The old woman said, "Go straight ahead. Baizhang then walked off. The old woman said, "What a fine master you are, yet you go away like that!
Baizhang returned and, ascending the hall, said, "I have thoroughly exposed this old woman for you all."
The Master held up his staff and said: "Soaring beyond measure—this is Zhaozhou’s Barrier. Calling out without being answered—this is the Tiantai Road.
This old woman has thorns filling the earth and dust stretching to the heavens; had she not encountered the Demon King, how could he have captured and defeated her?

Case: Master Yunmen said, "When light does not penetrate through, there are two kinds of illness.

First, being unenlightened in all places, as if there were something before one's face. Second, having penetrated through so that all phenomena are empty, yet there is still a lingering sense that something remains."
This, too, is a case where the light has not yet penetrated through. Furthermore, the Dharma-body also has two kinds of illnesses.
First, having attained the Dharma-body, one fails to forget the attachment to dharmas; one's own views still persist, and one falls into the side of the Dharma-body.
This is one illness. Even if you manage to penetrate through it, do not let it pass unexamined. If you scrutinize it closely, what essence is there? It is also an illness.
The Master held up his staff and said: "The traces of refined craftsmanship and the flaws of ultimate investigation cannot be discerned except by those with the eye of wisdom.

Case: Guishan asked Yangshan, "Suppose someone were to ask: 'All sentient beings have only a vast, wandering karmic consciousness with no fundamental basis to rely upon;

The Master held up the staff and said: "The father and son of Mt. Hui and Yang were indeed uniquely sober in their examination of others; yet I, Boshan, must ask them:

Study. Linji addressed the assembly, saying: "There is a true person of no station who is constantly entering and exiting before you.

As the monk hesitated, Linji leaped down from his meditation seat, seized him, and pushed him away, saying: "The true person of no station—what a dried-up shit-stick!"
The Master held up the whisk and said: "Linji’s spirit reaches the clouds and the sky; he is truly an outstanding man of character.

Case: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “I have only recently entered the monastic community; I beg the Master for instruction. Zhaozhou said, “Have you finished eating your congee?

The Master held up the whisk and said: "Zhaozhou was discerning within the decisive; this monk was decisive within the discerning. Truly, such a swift opportunity is difficult to encounter.

Case: Deshan ascended the hall and said, "When everything has been exhausted and cast away, even the Buddhas of the three periods of time have their mouths hung upon the wall.

The Master held up the whisk and said: "Standing alone and precarious, yet further employing intimacy. Beyond the Dharma there is no self, yet one still lacks the nostrils for a roar.
