A somersault through the void—how many times has it been performed? Upon a heap of withered leaves, one’s own brow and eyes are revealed. You should know that before the birth of your parents, the breath had not yet...

Come! The principle is likewise so. If you can penetrate this slight matter within, it is like a stone tiger on a layered crag sleeping while cradling its cubs; with a single roar, the mountains and peaks tremble. Will the golden-scaled dragon ever consent to leave the brine-pot?

Suddenly, when wind and clouds meet in harmony— *Note: The original text contains a play on words between "some small matter" (些子事) and the "tiger's cub" (兒), as well as the contrast between the "golden-scaled fish" (金鱗) seeking the vast ocean versus remaining in the "pickled pickle-pot" (醃虀甕). The imagery evokes the Zen themes of sudden awakening and the transcendence of mundane constraints.*
Behold the great function of soaring and leaping with majestic power; let the myriad phenomena listen to the beckoning and calling. The illusory dharmas born of conditions are all in vain;
on Vulture Peak there was a separate intent in the plucking of a flower. It brings to laughter the blue-eyed barbarian of those days.
To Layman Zhang Qinzhi:
When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? In the cycle of birth and death, there is no companion; the five aggregates and the sensory faculties all belong to Māra.
To subdue Māra, one must obtain the vajra-pestle; the essential body of the vajra is revealed in its majestic brilliance. The thief-demon...
Difficult to deliberate upon with others. Since antiquity, protecting life requires killing; once all are killed, one dwells in peace, reaching one’s native land.
The patriarchs have transmitted the True Dharma Eye; this lion cub was not born from a monkey. These fragmented verses and broken threads are the entirety of the family treasure.
The fierce Han has never made free choices; within the blink of an eye, the myriad phenomena are arrayed before him. With grand strokes he attains ease;
meeting people, he does not leak the true message. He smiles as he gazes upon the lotus all day long.
He showed Ni Qiongpǔ, the Court Lecturer:
"When the single breath does not come again, where exactly will you go? The great thousand-fold world system is gathered within the tip of a hair;
the majestic ancient road is free from all obstructions. Who dares to say, 'This is my dwelling place,' when facing the sun? Beneath Mount Jíyún, the four rattan canes sit and cut it off."

The spring breeze does not withhold its height; at the tips of the hundred grasses, one receives the direct transmission. Amidst the myriad flowers, one wanders at ease. Emptiness is not great, and dust is not small.
Among all things, none excel in the excellence of their emergence and dwelling. At the crossroads of the street, he awaits that person.
Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, content with warmth and fullness; I have fanned out until only a single spark remains in the cold hearth.
Utterly devoid of conscious thought and lacking spiritual penetration, I tread upon the very path by which I came; only then do I believe the clear pool is bottomlessly pure.
To Sun Ming, Jinshi:

When one breath does not follow another, where, after all, does one go? A man of wisdom should not perceive this through the signs of clarity. The vast heavens are suddenly opened, revealing the multitude of peaks;
having attained the Way, one drifts away like a soaring phoenix, soaring ten thousand *li* to behold the square and the round. Pure light.
It does not share the same mold as the marketplace; this was spoken personally by the Elder of Yaoshan: "The water is in the jar, and the moon is in the sky.
Its great function is majestic and beyond all boundaries; its movements and stillness are as rich and beautiful as spring. Walking alone in the Great Dharma, the realm is but the mind.
Who would boast of great or small within the void? The picking up of the flower fundamentally does not involve departure or subtlety.
Having scrutinized the ancient adept of Vulture Peak, one finds that by the seamlessness stupa there is much water and grass; deep within the dragon’s lair, the deer are fat.
To the Layman Lin Qian Shi:
When the breath no longer flows, where will you ultimately go? Recognize it at the very first step; though traversing ten thousand miles in all directions, you never depart from the sky.
Do not wait until the moment of parting to weep at the crossroads. If you wish to know the reaches of Huai and the banks of the Yangtze, they are interconnected.
The jostling throngs of chariots and horses are exhausted; scattered like drifting clouds, they vanish as one opens the eyes. The Lake of Heaven (Dongting) has no canopy, and the Dharma-body is cold.

What purpose is served by freezing the Dharma-body to death? On the opposite shore, there is no distinction between "other" and "self. In every atom and every world-system (*dharmadhātu*), all subtle traces are utterly severed.
Who says that brothels and wine shops are inaccessible? Steep cliffs and layered crags cannot be climbed. Yet one may expect to see waves upon the dry land;
The sound of the wind and the songs of birds proclaim the True Dharma. All is contained within the misty waters of Longmian.
To Layman Yang Lanshi:

When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? Since ancient times, the gate of compassion has never obstructed or rejected; the precious abode is not far—this is the time to hasten forward.
Transverse and vertical movement originally does not follow fixed rules: within light there is darkness, within darkness there is light; light and darkness...
After the consultation ends, they inquire about the journey; they snap off the horn on the head of the black dragon. Beside the coral branches, the water-stains are pungent.

Shaking off the entire body, one fashions emptiness and the uncanny; eyes, ears, nose, and tongue each demarcate their own boundaries. Smashing them to pieces and kneading them into a sphere—none of this matters at all.
One who buys for themselves must sell back to themselves; carrying water and hauling wood, one recognizes the Channel. From the beginning, within this, there is no intimacy or estrangement.
On what does the Buddha-dharma rely to abide in the deep mountains? Birds roost and clouds hide as the moon rises at its first appearance.
To the lay practitioner Hu Yongyin:
When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? This "head-word" (huatou) should be frequently raised;

by penetrating it thoroughly according to conditions before birth, the mountain stream and pine winds shall serve as dharma-talk. To gallop sideways or ride backward is no difficulty; throughout the oceans of lands...
Mount Sumeru is within a glance; numinous fungi and auspicious grasses flourish alongside the clouds. Exquisite trunks and celestial blossoms bear the chill of the dew.

Leisurely grasping his bamboo staff, he strikes the void until it rings; why would he deign to display such cleverness before others? At the two times of day, he partakes of porridge and rice as his daily routine.
Neither jeweled nets nor bright pearls are esteemed; I have traveled everywhere, never deceiving others. The winds and clouds beneath my feet I shall describe to you:
if you truly grasp the message within, you will live like a spirit amidst the realms of sense-faculties and objects.

To the Layman Zhongyin of Xi, who asked: "When one's breath ceases, where does one ultimately go? With eyebrows turned upside down, there is another path; with a sudden "clatter" on the ground, one awakens in a flash.
The person is in the deepest place of mist and clouds; the mind is like an ancient well, never ruffling a wave. This makes [the ignorant] laugh to scorn!
The Way-showing Old Woman of Mount Tai raises her fist, making it vividly clear; when she lets down her cloth bag, what can be done about her?

Facing one another, she moves freely without inhibition; in the moment of encounter, why discuss the limits of a single instant? Throughout the ten directions and three periods of time, there is no obstruction.

Pervading all, who can distinguish between mind and environment? Amidst the heaps of worldly toil, there is the fragrance of the wondrous lotus. Whether from the East or the West, it is in vain to proclaim it;
yet there is one further word that cannot be uttered—discussed only where no person is present.
To the three lay practitioners Xia Guangsheng, Yuanfu, and Shengsheng:
When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? When one can let go, one can also gather it back together. The mud beneath one's feet is deep and the water is likewise deep;
where the mud and water are deep, there is no place to rely. One need only straighten the iron backbone and strike through.
The boundary walls reach back to one's native village; having recognized the face prior to birth, the entire body breaks into a profuse sweat, cutting off all deliberation.

This profuse sweat circulates as a pure wind from antiquity. I dare say that among mountains and rivers there is not an inch of soil; moving freely in all directions, one does not fall into the silent mechanism.
The Martial Han has always taken great strides; he is sated by the Ox-Horn rice and Zhaozhou’s tea. When spring arrives in the gardens, every tree is in bloom.
If you further ask for the ultimate meaning of the Westward Journey, it is a life of simple serenity amidst white clouds and flowing streams.
I showed Layman Renfu: "When you take your final breath, where will you ultimately go? To sift gold from sand, do not be reckless; recognize the Real upon the mountain of the five aggregates.
From the beginning, it has never left its own gate. It is like catching a thief—you must see the stolen goods. Having obtained [this realization],...
When dealing with stolen goods, one must skillfully gauge and analyze the items present before the thief. A true son of the Empty Gate excels at this;

through illusory transformations amidst the dust-laden toil of the world, he sustains the life-force of wisdom. One must know that while karmic burdens exist, the nature remains pure and luminous; it cuts off the ten directions, leaving no passage for the wind of conceptualization to enter.
The earth turns and the heavens revolve—this is called Great Samādhi. Incense is burned in the furnace to test the power of reviving the soul.
Fragrant smoke coils and knots like clouds atop the peaks; one rides a stone tiger backward home at evening. Clapping hands, wandering leisurely, laughter and speech are fresh.
To the Zen practitioner Xuanzhao Kai:
When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? Treading upon it, every single thing is a treasury; clearly, the bright moon shines upon the golden sand.
Who would not behold this immeasurable radiance? You need only open your eyes to see the light; take up your staff and walk forth.
Seeking the stream, I loved the level path; I bumped into an old man with a long beard and a dark face. Only then did I realize that a fierce man knows no sentiment.
Turning my body, I stepped upon the crown of Vairocana; direct and unimpeded, I returned to self-reflection. Without asking for directions, I returned at nightfall.
One must know that dew makes the clothes cold; when the teeth are missing from the mouth, the wind cannot enter.
If one is willing to refrain from debating differences before others, yet gives rise to even a single thread of discriminatory thought, there will be mountain upon mountain and water upon water.
Revealing the single suchness:
when a Chan practitioner’s single breath does not return, where ultimately will they go? Pushed forward, they cannot advance; left behind, they cannot stay.
The mother-born eyes beneath the brows suddenly open: the flesh-ball is originally a treasury of bright pearls. Within the treasury of bright pearls, treasures are piled high; the earth trembles.
The heavens overturn and the echoes roar like thunder; those who are not the kinsmen of our own house have just now entered and are startled back out again.
Who among men has no blood beneath their skin? To whom can one speak of the warmth or cold of one’s own mind? Why labor to establish a flight of stairs in such a deliberate manner?
In a single thought of non-arising, one transcends all at once; the cliffside of the Patriarchs is as slippery as moss. A single phrase that strikes the vital point fulfills the original intent;
do not say in vain that there are countless billions of emanations—within a single speck of dust, there is indeed a Tathāgata.

To the Chan practitioner Jingxiu Zhen: When you take your final breath, where will you ultimately go? To raise this question is like threading through thorny brambles; when it cannot be unraveled, progress becomes difficult. Liberation requires skillful mastery;

then, one remains unstained amidst a thicket of myriad flowers. Before the eyes— *Note: The original text appears to be an incomplete verse or koan inquiry. The translation reflects the available text.*
Lacking sinews, one remains poor for a lifetime; pressed against the riverbank, one cannot move forward. Standing upright, one crosses the water and beholds the Great Man;
iron is not hard, nor is cotton soft. Upon entering the gate, first guard against the house dog; twist the cord and accord with the patriarch’s pivot.
Eighteen thousand miles of journey, its distance unrecorded; village songs and communal feasts in a spring day’s harmony. Amidst the deep green of the distant peaks, white clouds abound.
If one seeks to communicate the message through speech or silence, one has already lost out to Ling Xingpo of old.
To the Chan practitioner Cen Bo-huo:

When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? Directly entering and crossing at will, a horned tiger; fragrant auspicious grasses and numinous fungi transmit their scent in secret.
Amidst layered crags and steep cliffs, the pure wind is ancient. The household goods for enjoyment are present in every form—this is the true reality.
At first, he would not speak to others; then, suddenly, with a single "thump" of the staff upon the ground, he finally believed that there was a separate transmission within the Zen school.
A man of spirit does not borrow the strength of another; who would be willing to let the white days slip away in idle routine? Idle clouds and flowing waters pass by in mutual succession.
An ancient path, as straight as a brushstroke; one who recognizes this innate, austere form will find it as brilliant and pure as lapis lazuli.
What need is there to cultivate virtuous karma through many lifetimes? Such elegance shall surely emerge from a true scion of the house.
To Zen person Shimenyun:
When the breath no longer comes, where will you ultimately go? Enter directly into the state of non-receptacle, free from fear or dread.
If you are one of our own family’s seedlings, your heroic spirit possesses its own mother-born trousers. These mother-born trousers are not ordinary; they cling closely to the flesh.
Even with skin-deep conjecture, one measures according to his apertures to distinguish density and sparseness; yet there is another thread as long as a needle’s point.

If you can understand this, you may hide your body within the Big Dipper; ten thousand streams and a thousand currents all surrender their heads. The moment you give rise to deliberation, you are separated by the ends of the earth.
A jackal can never match the roar of a lion; from deep within the green willows comes the cry of a cuckoo. It awakens that person to attain freedom;
in the mountains, water and grass suffice according to conditions. He laughs as he releases the water-buffalo of Muzhou.
To the Zen practitioner Ciana:
When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? Upon the pure white ground, do not defile it with stains;
stride straight across and traverse sideways to reach your native land. Do not come to block the path to my ball gate. Through playful laughter and song, you shall recognize him. From of old...
The myriad dharmas are fundamentally suchness; the school of the Patriarchs possesses boundless elegance. I alone admire Yangqi’s three-legged donkey, scattering pearls before a purple silk curtain.
Worn-out vines and entanglements are all held in disdain; there is yet another path that pierces through the heavens.

The living word and clear function are as clear as one’s palm; once touched, they permeate the entire body like the sweetness of honey. To benefit sentient beings, he truly does not rely on the formalities of compassion or severity.
Throughout the villages of the three families, this has been deliberated upon: the water chestnut is sharper than a needle’s point—sharper still.
To the Zen practitioner Faguang:
When the single breath does not return, where will you ultimately go? Ten thousand *li* begin from the first step. To part the clouds and see the sun is not difficult;
but for the majestic and manifest wondrous function, you must turn back to yourself. To turn back to yourself, do not trouble yourself to look with the eyes. The frost is clear.
The dew is cold, the skull is frigid; suddenly, the sound of striking the bamboo vanishes. What remains are a thousand or ten thousand stalks.
To the practitioner who contemplates this:
when one’s breath no longer comes, where will they ultimately go? From this, the profound meaning of the double mystery arises. Running through Jambudvīpa...
Passing through myriad thousands of times, throughout kalpas, when has it ever left one's own self? To recognize what the countenance of one's own self is like:
the coarse robe is spread out, revealing half its mottled patches. Only after passing beneath precipitous cliffs and hanging crags does one finally know that there are tiered peaks upon the summit.
To Master Taichu: In the mountains of Huayan, the old man Taichu gazes upward with his two eyes, making the heavens and earth appear small. His eyebrows, flowing and relaxed, are extraordinary;
the sixteen-foot golden body is but a single blade of grass. Upon that single blade of grass stands a palace of jade; its essence is revealed in the golden wind. May you attain it.
Freedom. Liberation is the true aspect of the time of return. Not a single thread hangs from the alms-bag. We share the same province and the same county;
yet we are neither old acquaintances, nor kin, nor those who meet face-to-face. Having left the mundane world, you have come as if by prior appointment.

Your karmic机缘 (conditions) are suddenly different from how others see you. Others do not recognize the two rows of hidden storehouses. Many laugh at the neighbor’s young child for being wild. Samādhi.

Who among the hundreds of thousands has provided this commentary? For a time, you have won the radiance upon your brow. Having purely cultivated the three karmas, you cross over like a life-preserving bag;
your preceptual virtue is so clear and bright that all look up to you in admiration. I am ashamed that my worldly entanglements cannot be cast aside; on what day shall we meet again at Longmen?
There is no need to ask for directions at the crossroads; know that your lifespan is as vast as the sands of the Ganges. Mounting a mud ox backward, you blow the iron flute;
the white tuft of light shoots across how many Sumerus!

The Elder Dugou was shown the true treasure-trove of our house; with solemn care, he was willing to let go of the rope’s end. This great cause and condition for ending birth and escaping death depends on the person present being able to choose the superior path.
Body, mind, and the world are equal to flowers in the sky; the white ox in the open field grows ever stronger.
This carriage moves through the broad thoroughfare as pure breezes rise from all eight directions. An bottomless basket holds living snakes; meeting conditions, it does not leak the true mechanism.
Hard as cotton-wool, soft as iron; the staff is wielded freely in every direction. Clearly there are two mouths, yet neither has a tongue.
One must believe that after death and revival upon the precipice, a sudden form emerges like a map of mountains and seas. It turns back.
What realm is this of Heaven and Earth? At the first watch of the third watch, the golden crow shines forth.
This shows you, Upāsaka Poku, that you have recognized the true treasure-trove of our house. Ten-thousand-fathom cliffs must be climbed in person; one must be willing to sacrifice one’s very life.

The physical body serves as an excellent example for all people. Climbing mountains and wading through waters is their daily routine; grasping at waves and seizing the clouds, they must exert themselves.
Having penetrated the old monk’s flavorless phrase, how much of the profound and wondrous remains but dregs? Not lingering in the Dharma-body, one prizes the shifting of positions;
let the rain of flowers manifest auspicious signs from elsewhere. When the myriad phenomena are all swallowed in a single gulp, one casually casts them aside.
The fire-drill for the heavens is brought forth; a gust of barbarian wind strikes the face. An *utpala* flower is planted upon the tongue.
Every step of the journey must be reached through personal experience; do not speak in vain of Nanyue or Tiantai.

The Elder Shishu showed me that he does not dwell in mountain retreats but resides in the marketplace. He delights in forming virtuous karmic ties with donors; before his hermitage, carriages and horses throng naturally.
Each month he saves tens of thousands of living beings. Having encountered him in many lifetimes, I follow this "Hermitage Child" who brings relief to all.
Thus it arises. Magnificent and vast, he opens wide the Gate of Non-duality. Leaping from the abyss and stretching his wings, there is no end to his flight.
He does not begrudge this one body born of his mother; what hinders him from frequenting prefectures and counties? Not a grain of millet or a pinch of salt is kept for private use;

those with iron brows and copper heads behold their true Master. To act thus is to be truly unashamed of the marks of a monk; the Three Virtues and Six Harmonies are truly worthy of emulation. From beginning to end—
Do not alter your former conduct or concealment; go forth and serve as a model for the monastic community. You must further investigate thoroughly that which exists prior to birth;
apply the lash with great severity to those points you do not yet understand. Turn over the bowl as vast as heaven; see through it and realize it has never been worth a penny.
As I send these words to Chan Master Wuzhe upon Mount Luofu, I recall with longing the scenes of those years. Master Jingtai cleared the brush and built his hut on the shore of the sea;

he roamed at will atop the summit of Mount Luofu, where the Iron Bridge Peak borders the Jade Pond. At Shimen Fangguang, there was space for mats and desks; at the third watch, the sun rose from the sea.

The waters are crimson; turning over heaven and earth, one distinguishes the old from the new. Swallowing wind and clouds, one passes day and night. Where does the Master go now, and what does he seek?
Striding freely, he ascends the two stone pavilions with diligence. Looking down, the vast ocean appears like a mere drop. A thousand waterfalls are called the "Heroic Flow.

Beside the Bright Moon Altar, the precepts remain abundant. Slaying Buddhas and burning scriptures, he boasts of his vigor. His staff— *Note: The final line "錫杖" (staff) indicates the text likely continues with a description of the monk’s mendicant’s staff.*
The source is pure as it bathes the living dragon; at the precipitous Jade Goose Peak, one meets the Flower-Headed One. In the seventy-two caves, celestial music resounds;

the hundreds of thousands of plants and trees become jade pavilions. When the night is deep and the danger is extreme, turning back is difficult; kicking through the fingertip, one personally beholds the foot.

I too shall come in the future to walk these mountains; entering the depths of the forest, I shall heed no affairs of the world. Breaking off cassias and chewing on fungi, I shall let the years pass in leisure, occasionally gazing upon the clear azure waters that reflect my aging face.
To the Chan practitioner Jingxiu, who mourns his mother:
The bonds of affection and love drag one through countless kalpas; one need only have a sudden flash of insight to see one’s own mother.

If you attempt to distinguish between flesh and bone as true or false, you will surely find your hands and feet busy for many lifetimes. Do not let this one opportunity pass; strike the sounding skull—who is it?

Today I have personally encountered the conditions for spiritual friendship; one must quickly exert effort and apply the whip with vigor. The waters of craving and the mountains of emotion are inexhaustible;
who knows how many thousands of years we have wandered in saṃsāra? The mind of the Way-man does not lose its illumination; the pearl upon his brow shines with brilliant clarity.
He takes up his broken staff and stirs the great river; wherever it touches the silt and sand, all is treasure. Where, then, can worldly attachments remain?
This is my own mind. Turn over this bare flesh; do not seek it outside.

To the Chan practitioner Hengyi, I show that what remains unchanging through vast eons is called "constancy. Strolling with open chest, one enters the thorn forest. To eliminate all names and categories is called...
1. Standing alone on the peak ten thousand fathoms high, a flicker of a foot and a raise of an eyebrow let two or three fall.
To carry the burden without a body is not the ultimate point; one need only tread the ancient path where no monk is met. Earth turns and heaven revolves as if they never happened.

Wrapped in straw sandals at the corner of the *kāṣāya*, one occasionally picks out the sun’s lamp from the depths of the water. Beyond the railing, the idle person shares the colors of dawn; empty space fills [all].
Stifled as if in pitch-black darkness, he suddenly opens his two eyes like bronze bells. What need is there to wait for the future to question Maitreya?

This is the eternally unchanging mind; from the beginning, it has never sought outwardly. When the spring breeze blows into the mountain clefts, listen quietly as the branches announce the auspicious news.

The Master Qijing of Xihe is renowned as a venerable elder among the Chan practitioners of Zhejiang. Who does not possess the bright pearl of the ocean? From antiquity to the present, the "bowl-shaped" [mountain] has been passed down;
who is the hand that grasps the clouds and rides the waves? The flesh protuberance (uṣṇīṣa) remains hidden for many autumns, yet its radiance shines universally throughout the four directions.
The Divine Continent: Hearing and seeing turn back to one another as one discerns the essential point; eating and dressing, one attains freedom.
If you truly taste even a fraction of this flavor, you will stumble like a fool and be as if intoxicated. When meeting people, you are too lazy to speak of the mechanism before your eyes;

it is best to simply follow the crowd and join the ranks. For what reason have you come from Mount Bo-shan? Do not rashly conjecture about the sound of the tides on the waters of Chekiang. [Look at] your own heels.
Treading the path of one’s hometown, drenched in white sweat, one is buried alive.

To the Zen student Kuang’an, I show that thorough penetration without dependence is called "Kuang" (Expansion). When worldly attachments and obstructions are completely eliminated, and the mind is empty while the environment is tranquil, it is called "An" (Peace).
Peaceful. Only the realm, only the mind—difficult to compare by analogy. One need only raise an iron backbone; smashing through empty space is one’s true home.
Yunmen’s “moldy bread” and Niu-tou’s “ox-head rice”—only after eating them does one know their flavor is long-lasting. A thousand layers, a hundred turns, with no obstruction or mutual exclusion;
on this bare lump of flesh, the proclamation is revealed. Zhaozhou’s bridge over the stream is the same from ancient times to the present; it cuts off [all conceptualization].
Allowing donkeys and horses to pass; through perfect fusion and integration, the total function is revealed. With dusty faces and ash-smeared heads, awakening and delusion are both transcended.

When asked what the monk has accomplished, the clear breeze and bright moon fill the stream before him. This is the true enjoyment of the Chan practitioner; the nostrils of saints and commoners have always been shared.
With a broad stroke and a high sweep, five *liang* is light; sitting upright in silent stillness, a thousand *jin* is heavy.
The Buddha-dharma is a burden of afflictions; though there is no smoke or fire, it scorches the bones and chills the hair.
Once one morning this entire burden is cast off, turning soil into gold is altogether not difficult.
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi, Volume Sixteen;
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi, Volume Seventeen.
Compiled by Honghan, Dharma Grandson residing at Boshan.

Verses for Instruction Presented by the Head Seat and Dharma Grandson Hongyu (3): To Layman Wang Sheng’an Layman Wang Sheng’an, listen well: The Way is originally not a matter of cultivation. If you wish to cultivate it, you will only increase your delusion; If you do not cultivate it, you will only increase your afflictions. It is like a person who, having lost their way, Seeks a guide to lead them back home. Yet, even while seeking a guide, they have already lost their own path. How can they possibly find the way home? If you wish to attain the Way, You must first abandon all seeking. If you seek the Way within the mind, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the body, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eyes, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the ears, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the nose, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the tongue, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the body, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the mind, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the intellect, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the senses, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the objects of perception, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the six consciousnesses, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the three realms, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the four elements, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the five aggregates, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the twelve sense bases, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eighteen elements, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the twelve links of dependent origination, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eighty-four thousand afflictions, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the six paramitas, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the ten stages of a bodhisattva, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the four fruits of arhatship, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the three vehicles, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the nine grades of rebirth, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the three bodies of the Buddha, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the four wisdoms, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the five eyes, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the six supernatural powers, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the ten powers, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the four fearlessnesses, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eighteen unique qualities, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eighty minor marks, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the thirty-two major marks, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eighty thousand dharmas, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the three mysteries, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the four inconceivables, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the five gates of liberation, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the six perfections, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the seven treasures, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eightfold noble path, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the nine successive meditations, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the ten stages of the bodhisattva, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the eleven levels of the śrāvaka, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the twelve divisions of the scriptures, You will never encounter the Way. If you seek the Way within the thirteen ascetic practices, You will never encounter the Way. Look at the donkey! Having sought out even a trace of the flavor of the mattock, one lies amidst the clouds and whistles to the moon while planting pine saplings.

To show Wu Chang, the fertile field of Cao does not forget the personal entrustment of Vulture Peak; moment by moment, one must be taught to penetrate deeply into the wood, until the entire body bursts through the crown of the head.
Open! Six times six is originally thirty-six. The iron boat remains intact as the sea tides flow through. The moon sets, the sands grow cold, and the fishing is done.
If you can personally realize this within it, the bamboo flute will blow through the hollow reeds.

I show that Master Ding Lianlu, a scholar of the National Academy, has not forgotten the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. In the Pure Land of Precious Flowers, there is neither extension nor contraction. Below the eyebrows, the tip of the nose hangs down;
who can understand how one rows a boat upon dry land? The ferryman crossing in his double-hulled vessel has never been deluded; yet when one speaks of the source of the river, it is already lost.
I do not know. The snow fills my short raincoat, and the cold dream is shattered; I am startled to find myself a fishing master.

To Lin Ru-chong, the Fengchang, who has not forgotten the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak: "The familiar place shall become life, and life shall become the familiar place. Thus, take both the raw and the cooked into a single cauldron.
Frying. The lame tortoise and the blind turtle cry out, "Ten thousand blessings! Wherever one steps out the door, there is nothing but green mountains.
At evening, the traveler—idle yet not idle—opens the grain for the mortar to provide for his drunken eyes; he grinds it into a brick-mirror to reflect his withered face.

To Wén-sūn Zhōngmì of Wú, I show that you have not forgotten the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. In every instance and every dharma, there is the realm of radiant light. In the empty hall, amidst nothingness, a clap of thunder resounds;
the wild fox leaps into the den of the golden-haired lion. The golden-haired lion knows how to turn his body around; here it is clearly evident.
Obscured by causes, he spat out his fox-saliva only to enter the ranks of foxes; though he has left the mountains, he remains a mountain-dweller.

To show Wang Shudu, the Jinshi, that he does not forget the personal entrustment from Mount Ling, one must not overlook the carriage and horses on the broad highway, as yellow dust rises slowly to fill the heavens.

The limit. Rely on you to wipe away the vulgarity of the green mountains; the green mountains have no circumstance other than being clothed in autumn mist. Deer-grass and dragon-mushrooms are planted in the fields of jade.
There is only one year’s harvest yet to be gathered: the ancestral treasures scattered by the side of the Forbidden City.

Showing Shen De-yi, a filial and upright scholar, who did not forget the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. Having attained the Way, his steed-like spirit pursues the wind with full stride; galloping and trampling, he sees clearly.
Across ten thousand *li* of empty mountains, he seeks out ancient masters. Seeking men, the shadows of flowers fall in profusion. Who shall instruct him to report this jade girdle?
The patched skirt. There must be a place for further discourse upon departure. The clouds of Zhongshan resemble the clouds of Boshan.

To Chen Bensheng, the *xiao-lian*, he shows that one must not forget the personal entrustment of Vulture Peak. White rocks and gray pines are fit for striking the *zhu* lute; struck, they produce a single thread as fine as a needle’s point.
Pervasive. A thousand streams and ten thousand branches, observe the swirling eddies; white waves upon mountain peaks, dust within the sea. With no coin in one's bag, one buys spring all the more;
when the moon fills the coral branches, they reveal themselves spontaneously. Sitting cross-legged, one should surely laugh at those from kalpas past.

To Xu Liuxu, the Xiaolian: Do not forget the personal entrustment from Mount Ling; how could the Gate of the Patriarchs be entered by relying on others? A hero smiles at such men from beneath his eyes;
the ancient path of pure wind is free of detours. In Zen study, one must first recognize the mind’s stillness; once the brocade carp becomes a dragon—
In the space of a leap, the leather bag emits light and worldly attachments are exhausted. With a faint air, he uses words and phrases to depict the streams and mountains.

To Cao Qingzhi, the Court Musician, he shows that one must not forget the personal entrustment from Vulture Peak. When practicing Chan, do not settle within the state of Chan; on that very day, one knows only the hilt of the sword.
Long has it been; only now do I realize that the gate of the ball is double-layered, and that the withered stump was never truly a withered stump at all.
At every point, the wind shakes the white jade banner; ten thousand *li* away, the clay ox gallops off after its own shadow. The azure clouds, beyond restraint, fill the spring river.

To Chen Yujia, the Guangwen Teacher, who does not forget the personal entrustment at Mount Ling: atop the peak of Duanya, within a thatched hut of yellow reeds, he cuts off the ten directions and beholds the spring breeze;
parting the clouds at night, he gazes upon the Valley of a Thousand Flowers. Mounted upon Yangqi’s three-legged donkey, even where he does not encounter "him," there it is.
"Meeting him. Unfastening the cloth bag, he invites others to look. His wondrous function applied to the immediate moment is indeed no different [from the source].

To show Zhang Shihua, the Military Commissioner, that he does not forget the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak: "For ten years he has prepared the traveler's robes in advance; yet the traveler cannot avoid being caught by the journey."

The Saddle. To avoid being caught in haste at the final moment: With embroidered banners casting shadows of smoke and azure oil-chariots, He lets loose the "tortoise-nosed" snake of the South Mountain.
If you say the entanglements are not yet severed, A single cup of pure offering—Zhaozhou’s tea.
To show that Senior Officer Zhou Yuanzhi does not forget the personal entrustment at Mount Ling: The cowherd boy rides home on his calf under the bright moon.

Before the time when man and ox are no longer seen, Do not follow the green grass across the level plain. After the rain, the fragrant grasses mark the village ahead; The cowherd’s flute sounds for no reason.
Severing the soul, he departs for the ancient, desolate temple; everyone helps lift up the broken sand-basin.

To Liu Douchu Sima, I show that the personal entrustment from Vulture Peak has not been forgotten. Moving freely through emergence and disappearance without constraint, the traces of the idle clouds vanish into the vast heavens.
The soil. From of old, both Māra and the Buddha have been kinsmen. It is easy to release life, but difficult to take it. Within the burning house, the jackals howl;
yet one sits upon the white ox-cart in the open air. Precious bells and pearl nets shimmer as the night sky grows cold.
To Wu Chun, Grandee of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices:
Never forget the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. Within this almsbowl are a thousand measures of grain; swallowing a single grain whole, the teeth and gums are fragrant.
Yet one laughs at the hungry man who truly has an empty stomach. From where does this single grain originally arise? The field of the mind within the great chiliocosm is vast and open.
Yet all is level. Last night there was a "rain for planting seedlings" [a light rain]. One should go toward the green willows to listen to the dawn orioles.

To show that Ye Yi’s formal visit did not forget the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak: how could a flower-seeking bee lodge in a hollow branch? It must bore its way through the silver mountains and iron walls.
In the midst, his household seems like an insentient object. When the field opens, observe those ascending the dais as they choose the Buddha.
Do not say it is difficult to attain the degree of "emptiness of mind. Kick the monkey to death and bind the ghosts; who knows what office the Bodhisattva holds?
He spoke to Qiu, saying: "Contemplate the purity of the palace;

do not forget the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. In the single phrase of Amitābha, there is neither the conventional nor the ultimate. When the cord of the prayer beads snaps, the sound of the Buddha vanishes.
Bianhe cut open the jade of Mount Jing; it is clearly like a precious mirror reflecting a thousand lamps. To select leaves and seek branches is my [delusion]."
Never before has one recognized the true offering of burning the hermitage; the clay ox wags its tail as it passes through the window-lattices.

To Li Zai-pu, the distinguished scholar, he shows that the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak has not been forgotten: the ceremonial banner is broken, the bamboo of Xiao and Xiang is bent, and the gate of the true mark opens in silence.
Yet, with short robes and a tattered straw hat in the realm of gold, the river breeze is languid and the Dharma-body is cold. The river rain is piercingly clear as the night has not yet ended.
Do not mistake the cry of the cuckoo for the song of the oriole; amidst the myriad flowers, the udumbara blooms.
Showing that the leaves are white within the inner hall, one does not forget the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. I hope you will listen to the Song of Non-arising:
a handless person plays it for earless listeners. Gathering together our former close kin, where can we ask for another direction? A single piece of empty heart is chosen.
The Buddha-field: beat the drum and see who acts as master. Angling for fish was originally the work of Xie Sanlang.

To show me that Senior Censor Jisheng has not forgotten the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak: you pluck the strings while I blow the flute; together we form a single melody to offer to the assembly.
Life arises; the flowers of Brahmā rain down to become grain and crops. It is turbid when stirred and lacks fragrance when burned. To catch a thief, one must have the actual stolen goods.
A washbasin is kicked over at the break of dawn. The name "Lamp-Transmitter" is interspersed among the ranks of monks.

I show you, Zhou Sheng, Military Commissioner of the Capital, that the personal entrustment at Mount Ling has not been forgotten. At noon, by the empty window, I trim a bright candle; before the kitchen hearth, the clever housewife ponders deeply.
I laugh at myself for being able to cook rice-gruel when there is no rice. The various devas share the same vessel but eat different meals; the golden talisman behind the elbow draws near.
Already worn smooth. The horse’s hooves resemble clouds, the bow resembles the moon. Tonight, the General shall descend upon the Three Han kingdoms.

To the Fangshi and the Great Academy, he shows that he has not forgotten the personal entrustment from Mount Ling. Before one's eyes, the green mountains are entirely not "things"; one has passed straight through the midst of thorns and brambles.

At that time, what need is there for the horizontal rush or the direct entry? A whirlwind strikes with the "eight characters" (the eight trigrams). Wherever the jeweled net and golden cords touch, they open wide.
Ten thousand valleys and a thousand crags are naturally warmed by spring; the hare's light and the morning dew protect the pearl in its womb.

To Layman Ji: You, a householder, have not forgotten the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. You urge on the ox, riding backward upon it; repeatedly you blow the iron flute upon its back, and with every note, the melody of the Song of Non-arising emerges.
Who can join in the chorus of this Song of Non-arising? Only the stone man knows how to keep time with the wooden clapper.
A Song: Wandering throughout China, I return late; beneath the scholar’s robe lies the Ancient Amitābha.

To Chen Minzhao, a student of literature, he reveals that he has not forgotten the personal entrustment from Vulture Peak. The jade sprout has blossomed afar at Liuyang, where the Buddha raises the disgrace of our house and presses upon us.

Busy! To ensure that for a thousand lifetimes one suffers from the poisoned drum, yet in a thousand lifetimes it is perfected in a single morning. The sound of the poisoned drum rises as ten thousand horses lead the way;
suddenly, Zishao clarifies the principle of things: from the purple clouds of the golden hall, a dark fragrance is transmitted.

I show you that the layman who has attained this has not forgotten the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak. What hinders one in daily life from both plowing and reading? Within these books, the hearts of the sages and worthies are fully revealed;
it is much like a fertile field yielding fine grain. Both sages and worthies come from the site of enlightenment; the lineages of Confucianism and Buddhism are inseparable.
Frivolous conjecture. Having grasped the meaning of the flower and the smile, the whisk of tortoise-hair dances through the three terraces.

To the Chan practitioner of Shan Water, he shows that the personal entrustment at Vulture Peak has not been forgotten; the waves are clear in samādhi as silver swans bathe. Since they have not understood how to ride it backward...
Ox. When tears fall from the stone man, it is the melody of longing; longing is difficult to express when dreams first part. Half is thinking of you, half is resenting you.
If the pipa could speak it out, the tips of the fingers would surely manifest clouds upon the incense burner.

Compiled by Honghan, Dharma Grandson residing at Boshan.
Verses on Instruction Collected by the Head Seat and Dharma-Descendant Hongyu (4):
To Layman Liu Zidu.
Where there are no traces, do not hide your body; the clear river has been fished dry of leaping scales.

Where the body is hidden, there are no traces; on both banks of Huating, flowers lie in profusion. Bursting through the void, there is another heaven; deep within the green willows, the grasses grow lush.
You must further examine the affairs of daily life: the lame donkey is in the back garden.
I show Layman Zhilín that the minds of sentient beings and the Buddha are without distinction. If one does not understand this Great Principle, one must vow never to cease effort.

Once the original person is recognized, one suddenly awakens to non-arising and only then rejoices. Children and grandchildren gather in the ancient site of practice; every step taken must first reach the destination.
One's original home is the face one had before parents were born; putting on clothes and eating meals is the daily routine.

To demonstrate awakening and establish the will for practice upon the meditation seat, one must be resolute and outstanding—just like fine jade that requires repeated carving until it is polished through and through on all eight sides.

At that time, when the work is accomplished, one first attains the title of "One Beyond Learning" (aśaikṣa). Letting go of worldly attachments, one simply rests. Why should the green mountains cause a person to grieve?
The herdsman’s whip is gathered back into the treasury of the bright pearl; forth is released the water-buffalo of Mt. Mui.
Showing Wu Guanwo, Palace Counselor: The fly-whisk sweeps freely beyond the kalpas; each time it is brandished, it is ever new. The oil-flask exposes the guest who came at dawn;
the tea-talk yields to the man who returns his salutation. The filial son’s wine-induced madness delights the rebellious child; the sword-swinging shatters the nest, verifying the truth.
The loyal minister does not refuse to plant bamboo again once the pole is exhausted; he rejoices in finding the leaping scales of the fish from Huating.
To Layman Jiang Xitai:
The Holy Way has no dependence and makes no distinctions among people. Why must one sever greed and anger upon entering the gate? The moon is full within a silver bowl, containing the autumn.
Bi: Dew-soaked pine waves carry the morning clouds; within the pure realm, it takes but a single thought, yet upon the path of saṃsāra, how many lifetimes have passed?
The pivot of inquiry suddenly shatters the dream of Jambudvīpa; I shall describe this auspicious grass and wondrous sprout for you.
I show you, Chan practitioner Zhanru:
the perfect clarity is profound and boundlessly wondrous. To engage with it even as much as a fine hair is already to be caught in the dust.

When the entire great earth is revealed as a world of silver, where else could one seek the Golden Body? Cease speaking of delusion; do not attempt to distinguish the true. Know only that from one horse, three are born.
Yin. What is there in this pure breeze that sweeps the earth? Laughing, I watch the parrot pass through Xiqin.
To the layman Jiang Yi-zhou, I show:
Where on the banks of the Maṇi River shall one seek? One must search directly beneath the jaws of the black dragon; with a shout, turn the swift current—this requires valor!
Decisive! Drying up the vast ocean, he roams at will; grasping clouds and crashing waves with but two hands. He overturns mountains and empties the abysses with a single head.
Beneath his brows, the unobstructed eye suddenly opens, its radiance shining universally upon the four continents.
To Layman Zhang Xinggong:
You cast your body across the universe without obstruction; you exert all your strength to push back the mountains beyond the mountain.

Failing to distinguish the golden light from precious jade, you vainly chase after pebbles while the ten directions crumble away. Having escaped the trap and net, you leap into the source of spiritual vitality; in an instant, you transform like wind and cloud.
This is the essential meaning transmitted through the Caodong school; for your sake, I have revealed it in full detail.

To show you, Lord Prefect Xiao Ruozhuo, that one should not pursue external forms but observe the true mark (*dharmatā*), the mysterious mechanism alone reveals its face beyond the gates of the senses. This treasury of ineffable words flows forth through the ages.

Ancient and radiant, the true light of dreams penetrates the great void. The stone woman embroiders flowers in the sky and yet bears fruit; the wooden man strikes fire and a fish is born from the flames.
The source is wondrously pure, beyond both "is" and "is not"; when welcoming guests and receiving visitors, its essence remains as it is.
Receiving guests with a body as it naturally is—why labor to climb a tree to seek fish? The numinous mind illuminates the shadows of mountains and rivers;
the eye of wisdom surveys all phenomena as empty. Joyfully planting grass, one points to the ground; picking up a flower, a smile remains upon the face.
Now, having torn open the mother-born countenance, the eyebrows and eyes remain, yet they are not that person.

Showing Layman Huang Xuanshi how to transcend the dust and remain untainted by the stench of the poisonous dragon; in the ways of the world, even a wild goose feather is equally light. Within this field of illusion, who is "me"?

Within the flash of a lightning shadow, what constitutes "sentiment"? Having finished reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, one knows that emptiness is the end; upon ascending to the Jewel Place, one realizes true love.
The road is level; from of old, the Gate of Perfect Penetration has been grandly opened. I imagine purple clouds rising beneath your feet, O Reverend Chique-xuan.

You grasp the meaning of the Plucking of the Flower with perfect realization; you re-examine the mystery of the Precious Mirror. You propagate the Dharma to manifest the True Command, and skillfully employ the authentic transmission to verify its efficacy.
Steep cliffs are lush with spring green; numinous flowers bear the evening mist. Holding the myriad phenomena before the window, he stamps through the sky reflected in the water.
To the Zen practitioner Guryeok, who has traveled through all lecture halls and come to study flavorless Chan: he clears clouds to plant purple taro and leads water to grow blue lotuses.
Mist rises from the trees in the deep valley; dry firewood produces little smoke. The pine wind and the night moon face one another—no coin is required.
To the Layman Jin Canyu: In daily affairs there is no difference;
avoiding clamor only makes it more difficult. After the meal, one sings of the length of the day; when the candle is spent, one laughs at the end of the watch.
All things remain as they were; myriad phenomena are entirely idle. As soon as one gives rise to discriminatory thoughts, one knows how many mountains lie between.

To the Layman Kuibiao, who possesses a gathering of the two types of faith: for both the ordinary and the sage, there is no divergence. Letting it forth, there are only three essentials; drawing it back, it is but a single speck of dust.

Do not follow the transformations of others; do not allow yourself to be muddled by confusion. Once you recognize the treasure within your robes, why worry about poverty that penetrates to the very bone?
This accumulation of merit from the mind of faith is truly a lotus born from fire. Through vast eons it has never been otherwise; in this life, fortunately, the conditions have met.
Unveiling the net of the mundane realm, the seal shatters the heavens reflected in the water. Most joyful is the vajra-jewel; its radiance illuminates the great trichiliocosm.
To the lay practitioner Gong Keji, it is shown:

what could serve as an oar in the sea of suffering? A sincere heart can indeed deliver one. The breeze of compassion clears the waters of one's nature; the sun of wisdom shines resplendent in the midst of heaven.
The majestic features of the Flower Treasury adorn the body; Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa stands before one’s eyes. One must know that within the realm of dust, a blue lotus blooms amidst raging flames.

To the lay practitioner Li Xuyun: this single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. By the willows on the bank and the flowers on the crags, the Dharmakāya is revealed. How many times have you sought it deep within the lush green willows?
Look! It stands upright, not stained by a single speck of dust.
To layman Liu Zidu, I present this one phrase as a *huatou*:
"Straight as a bowstring. How many travelers cannot advance a single step? If you would enter, you must fix your eyes upon it.
Look! Deep within the clouds of incense, one penetrates the profound mystery.
To Layman He Shi: "What is the meaning of this phrase?
A single word is as straight as a bowstring; having fished the entire Yangtze River, he has caught the crimson-scaled dragon. Stepping down from the entanglements, all fetters are severed.
Severed. Transcendent and free from entanglement, ever-new with each passing moment.

To the lay practitioner Wang Yuanchun, I present this single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring: "Behold the sun-bright refined gold face-to-face. Having passed through the crystal palace, one walks on.
Depart! Before the gate there still stands a jade balustrade.

To show Master Zhuo Wuliang the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. When the pearl is clear, the water is naturally pure; one thus penetrates and beholds the original true face.
Upon seeing this, one finally realizes that the notions of self and other have no bearing on reality.
To layman Chen Minzhao, he presented a single phrase for contemplation:
"The bowstring is straight; the fragrant elephant gallops about, losing its majesty. Cut off the turbulent waves and observe yourself."
In the sandalwood grove, the phoenix soars. To Layman Zhang Xinggong, he showed that a single phrase about waves is as straight as a bowstring.
A drop of water stirs a high spirit; several *zhang* of waves emerge and submerge amidst the clouds and mist beyond measure.
As for measurement: what can one do with flowers in the sky or a mirage?

To the lay practitioner Yang Zhongyi, he showed the single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring: "Having wandered throughout Jambudvīpa, I know no one; I strike it directly at the tip of the staff."
He has deeply realized that discerning pain and pleasure is the critical pass.
To Layman Changqing, he showed that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Ambrosia comes down from the heavens; he personally turns the eight-cornered millstone.
Turning: infinite tree-seeds planted leaning against the clouds.

To the lay practitioner Wenxian, he showed the single phrase of the meditation topic as straight as a bowstring: "It is not an ox, nor is it a donkey; its hooves, horns, skin, and hair have all vanished."
Exhausted. The pearl at the crown of the head is vividly revealed.
To the lay practitioner He Yunliang, I show this single phrase of the meditation topic as straight as a bowstring: "The lame cat sleeps soundly, snoring. At midnight, who walks the path with me?
Speech: Amidst the shadows of moonlight flowers, we indulge in pure conversation.

To Layman Yao Linqing, I show this one phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring. As you advance, how can you know the road will not be difficult? Should you catch even a slight favorable breeze, it shall urge the traveler forward.
It is well. With a serene and detached mind, pass through the three rapids.
To C hen Feibai, the lay practitioner, I show this one phrase of the *huatou*:
"Straight as a bowstring. As for the point of entry, you should follow it from the side of the attendant; therein, you will further know how to employ wisdom through both stillness and movement.
Pulling out [the weeds]. The gate and courtyard are high and steep, as transmitted through ancient and modern times.
Master Shi Fan Er Pei, the lay practitioner, said:
"A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; it is difficult to set foot in the midst of a rapid torrent. One must pass through the Palace of Radiant Night."
The lining: "Severe frost penetrates to the core of one's heart in the sixth month.
To Layman Deng Zhique:
A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Fish swimming in the water, crows on the tree—suddenly, beneath the eyebrows, the pure and white is revealed.
With eyes smiling at the chaotic dust-lands as tangled as hemp, he shows me that the layman’s *huatou* (critical phrase) is as straight as a bowstring.
On the path of birds and the road of sheep, one may travel; traveling until the water ends and the mountains are exhausted.
In this state, the vast expanse of heaven and earth is of one age.
To show equality, the Governor’s pivotal phrase is as straight as a bowstring.
Jewel nets and fragrant clouds are flowers before the eyes; having pierced through the ice mountains and the snow, one arrives.
The Cave: Meeting, let us drink Zhaozhou’s tea. When showing the way, the single phrase of the Gongyuan candidate is as straight as a bowstring;
it is like the roar of spring thunder awakening the hibernating dragon—how could any conceptual understanding be permitted even in the slightest?
Presently, in good conduct, one must trust that the tracks of the chariot have left no trace.

To Yao Chunfu, the贡元 (Gongyuan) scholar, I present this single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring. When the pivot of the mechanism is activated, its response is inexhaustible; know this to be the true manifestation of your own self.
As for "measure": from the four directions and eight corners, a pure wind arises.

To show Zhang Shu’s words as the贡元 (Gòngyuán) *huatou*, a single phrase straight as a bowstring—wherein the conceptualizations of ordinary and sage do not obstruct the chest. Treading alone upon the Great Way, what realm is there?
The realm: riding an iron horse backward through the void.

To the lay practitioner Qi Li Hou, he showed that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. As karmic consciousness is worn away, it is like the frost of the sixth month; one opens one's eyes amidst the thicket of afflictions.
Look! The leather bag releases all the purple-gold light.

To the layman Qi Ji-yu, he shows the single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring. It compels the living fish and snake to transform into a dragon; the great earth, mountains, and rivers are reduced to dust.
At the end, blood splatters from his eyebrows, reddening the Brahma Heaven.

To the lay practitioner Hu Kangsheng, he shows the single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring: swift and fierce, the wooden horse neighs as it gallops, treading upon ten thousand valleys and a thousand peaks.
Pervasive. Plucking a *maṇi* jewel from atop a coral branch, he shows the single phrase of the *huáitóu* (critical phrase) for Layman Ningsheng:
as straight as a bowstring. The Patriarch’s command is fully upheld; this is the profound mystery beyond the ordinary. Do not seek divination within the realm of conceptual thought and words.
Crossing over. A single stroke at the head of the path leads straight to the home garden.

To the lay practitioner Shifang Yi, this one phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. When a person comes from an ice mountain or a snow cave, the seasons are no longer like those of the mundane world.
The realm: peach blossoms fill the garden in full bloom in the ninth month.
To Master Dai Shiqi, I say:
the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; the words before the cypress tree in the courtyard are most intimate. Walking along the side of the narrow wooden bridge—
Pass! A man of thorough understanding—how could he deign to inquire at the frontier passes?
To show the single phrase of the *huatou* from the assembly with Master Tao:
"As straight as a bowstring; pouring from the jar, clouds arise—this too is idle. If the Buddha-dharma were derived from intellectual understanding...
Entering, at Shaolin, he did not set his mind at ease.

To Layman Yao Shenfu, he showed a single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring. Only when merged with it does one know the nightless sky. The road carries the azure clouds; the clouds carry—
The Moon: A bodiless man sits before the desk-mountain, showing Liu Yinping, the provincial champion, the single phrase of the meditation topic as straight as a bowstring.
After the meal, he frequently pours the tea of Old Zhao; leaning on his staff, he joyfully follows the flowing stream.
Departing into the deep forest without a companion, one watches the flying crows.
To the lay practitioner Liu Junhan, I show this single phrase of the *huatou*:
"Straight as a bowstring. Having traversed the three thousand worlds and the great chiliocosm, when you turn your body around, what realm is there?
The Realm: Outside the night-bright curtain, the moon hangs in the sky.
To Liu Liuhé, the lay practitioner, I show this one phrase of the *huatou*:
straight as a bowstring. It merges into the numinous source, beyond the reckoning of years. If you recognize that your own mind is fundamentally...
The Buddha—where else would one seek the Golden Immortal?

To the lay practitioner Liu Erjing, he showed this single phrase of the *huatou*, as straight as a bowstring. The Sanskrit and the Chinese do not differ in meaning; it sweeps away all the idle bones of the world.
Dong. "The clear breeze and bright moon fill the courtyard.
To layman Liu Erjing, I show this one phrase of the *huatou*:
straight as a bowstring—red dust at the bottom of the water, fish upon the mountain; the cloth bag gathers them all.
Exhausted. Joyfully sitting in full lotus upon coral branches.

To the Chan practitioner Dongru, the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring: "In the midsummer heat, frost within the fire. You must believe that there is nothing else before your eyes.
The Dharma: When the mountain stream is deep, the handle of the ladle naturally lengthens.

To the Chan practitioner Weimi, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Meeting on a narrow path, there is no need to ask about the journey; beneath one's feet, there is originally nothing to hook or entangle.
The lasso: pulling crosswise and binding straight, there is no need for alarm.

To the Chan practitioner Huelin, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Having delivered all sentient beings, the Buddha is a demon; having pierced through both barriers of demon and Buddha.
It passes. The "Yangchun Baixue" (The Spring Breeze and the Snow) harmonizes with the "Ba Ge" (Barbarian Song).

To the Chan practitioner Cishui, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Upon waking from the dream, one joyfully beholds the spring beyond eons. Throughout the fields, oxen and sheep have their fill of water.
Grass. Do not let it trample the clouds atop the ridge.
To the Zen practitioner Zongbo, I show this:
the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. When the eyes are open, one must know the moment they are closed; there is no attachment to either extreme of light or dark.
In this place, he plays the iron flute upside down while chanting new poems.

To the Zen student Shui Cheng, he shows that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Taking up his staff, he seeks the stream and attains freedom; he stumbles upon the wooden man opening his mouth.
Question: Without speaking or smiling, he points to the water flowing eastward.

To the Chan practitioner Xuancan, he shows that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Drinking water and seeing it become ice—treat this as a matter of course. As soon as the staff is raised, three or two [steps are taken].
Step forward. How many rains of flowers fall upon the human world?

He said: "O Zen practitioner who understands the 'one phrase' of the *huatou*, it is as straight as a bowstring; go directly to the highest story of the multi-storied tower, and the myriad koans will be reduced to dust."
Shattered! Who dares to call this the *Continued Record of the Lamp*?

To the Chan practitioner Jingshan, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; eating and wearing clothes is the most supreme vehicle. Within this, do not give rise to discrimination.
Contemplation. Where the practitioner walks, fire melts the ice.

To the Chan student Zhonghe, he showed that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring: "The mountains are naturally green, and the waters are naturally blue. One’s livelihood does not depend on others.
Attained. The clear breeze and bright moon are fellow practitioners.
To the Chan practitioner Shidaoan, I say:
the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Since you have no mind, I too shall rest. The adornments of the Flower Treasury are originally complete.
Sufficient. Piercing through the jewel-net, there is no seeking elsewhere.

To the Chan practitioner Hongqi, he showed that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring: "Who is it that arises from conditions? Who is the Real? Sitting and cutting off both extremes, there is not a single speck.
Matter. Before the courtyard, one should look upon those who smile at the flowers.

To Zen practitioner □□, I show that this single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. When the ways of the world are in turmoil, how should one act? Directly enter into the midst of the ten thousand flowers.
Pass beyond; only when not stained by even a trace does one begin to penetrate through the entire body. When Chan Master Chang was about to pass into nirvana, he said:
"A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Do not concern yourself with the faults or virtues of others. How swift it is at the brink of birth and death!"
The direct path: once the doubt-mind is pulverized, there is no more deliberation.

To the Zen student Zhìhuā, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; the "True Person of No Rank" wears his leather boots backward. Walking until the water runs out and the mountains end.
In every place, the entire body is entirely Buddha.

To the practitioner Huiseng, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; what leisure mind is there to drum up right and wrong? Burst through the mass of doubt, and your dreams will be clear.
In the inner chamber, it is difficult to encounter one another to discuss the subtle nuances of parting.

To the Zen practitioner Zhanzhi, I show that a single phrase of the meditation topic is as straight as a bowstring. When the plum is ripe, what need is there to labor further to seek its pit? Once the sourness and astringency in the mouth have been spat out entirely.
As for flavor, there should be a subtle fragrance arising from one’s teeth and gums.
To the novice Chan practitioner Xiaozhi, I say:

A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; the orchids and calamus in the secluded valley are more fragrant than ever. When the waves subside and the waters are level, people [are at peace].
Speech: The mandarin ducks and wild ducks naturally form their own rows.

To those who practice the small stopping of Chan, a single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a taut string. To take it up directly is already late; before the birth of one's parents—[what was there?]
Look! No need to open your mouth; it is precious to know beforehand.

To the Zen practitioner Cao Yin, he showed that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring: "The Buddha is an old bhikṣu from Vulture Peak. With his hand, [he pointed] to his own head.
Touching upon it—there is no need for the spiral topknot of elegance.

To the Zen practitioner Xuanjing, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; thus one gains the living waters of Lingyuan, branching out without distinctions of high or low.
Conceptualization. Once the channel is formed, why must one scrutinize it in detail?

To the Chan practitioner Ruiyun, I show that this single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. To penetrate through worldly toil, these words are most intimate. Having gathered dry wood, one boils the living.
Water: pouring it out oneself and drinking from it oneself, one does not interfere with others.

To the Chan practitioner Hengru, I show that this single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Amidst wind and rain that never cease, he has finally reached home; yet he laughs at the donkey in the back garden eating.
Grass. As the setting sun shines from the west, its shadow slants askew.
To Layman Ge Huanbo, I show this one phrase of the *huatou*:
"As straight as a bowstring. "Finding peace of mind on a snowy night is not the mind itself. Behold the man of old, Ganmu!
Guest: On the road to Shitou, the cement is deep.

To the Chan practitioner Chunsu, I show that the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring: a lantern-ball upon the water, a lotus in the fire; it pierces through the snow-cave and the ice-mountain.
Pass on! At the very end of Chang’an, apply the whip once more.
To the lay practitioner Jiang Da, show that single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring. How deep is the yellow mud beneath one’s feet? Cast off the greasy, sweat-stained shirt entirely.
Exhausted. From him, one is tossed about and finds no concern.

To the lay practitioner Yuanxiu, he showed the single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring: "By day there is no toil, by night there is no sleep. Since antiquity, there has been no dot upon the tip of the nose.
Qi! Why need one go out of one's way to crave meat and pungent flavors? To the lay practitioner Cheng Junjian, I present this single phrase of the *huatou*:
"The bowstring is straight; returning home by way of the road is too dull. Throughout kalpas, there has never been the slightest change.
Easy. Why must one needlessly overstep the rules?

To the lay practitioner Ruihan Shi, I present this single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring: "The eighteen boys still cannot stop laughing; they have found a priceless jewel in a pile of dung."
O Treasure! How much joy, how much sorrow?

To the Chan master Juehai, he showed the single phrase of the *huatou* as straight as a bowstring—falling not within the realm of discursive thought, it is beyond the second tally. He topples Mount Sumeru and puts on his straw sandals.
Run! On the crown of Vairocana it is as slippery as oil.
To the assembly of Zen practitioners:
the single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. Floating clouds in the sky, flowers in a mirror—having seen this, do not give rise to thoughts of the extraordinary.
Contemplation: From the beginning, black beans have never sprouted;
a single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring. In this very moment, being without mind, one sees the original source. One must hold fast to the dry wood even more firmly;
the road to Mount Heng is as slippery as moss.
The single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; though earth and heaven may overturn, the mind remains unmoved. There is but one way of life:
following conditions, the deeper one enters, the more profound it becomes known.
A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; the deaf hear the sound of the Dharma being preached. When the clouds and waters have run dry, the song and dance end;
the Great Road of Chang’an is vast and level.
A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; this fundamental matter is clear, yet not permitted to be known. Should one stir even slightly, one encounters the medicinal taboo;
who would be willing to debate its profound compassion apart from words?
A single phrase of the *huatou* is as straight as a bowstring; hearing it spoken is no less intimate than meeting face-to-face.
Though the wind may be calm and one seems at leisure, there is still no rest—how could one fail to pity the golden-scaled fish leaping in the living water?
A single phrase of the head-word is like an iron stake; deep within the green clouds lies a family tradition. When meeting, there is no need for further explanation;
everywhere is the spring wind and the willows under the sky.
A single phrase of the *huatou* is like an iron stake; from within death, one seeks a living person. The six sense-faculties are pulverized and gathered into a single mass;
the *utpala* flower blooms throughout the entire world.
A single phrase of the head-word is like an iron stake; even amidst myriad circumstances, it renders them all void.
With not a trace of mud or water upon one's heels, pack the traveling bag and cross over the old mountains.

A single phrase of the *huatou* is like an iron stake; though one travels three thousand miles, the stride remains as it was at the start. From the beginning, the mind-dharma has had no external objects;
when the entire earth is gathered in, it is but a single thatched hut.
A single phrase of the *huatou* is like an iron stake. What is the news within movement? Not a hair’s breadth remains as it follows birth and death.
It brings to laughter the Lady Ling Xingpo of old.
A single phrase of the "head-word" is like an iron stake; when plucking the pearl from the jaws of the black dragon, one need only disregard danger and death.
Only upon gaining entry does one realize the marvel of transcending the world.
A single phrase of the *huatou* is like an iron stake; amidst the turmoil of sensory realms, the essence remains as-it-is (*tathatā*).
It requires only that you recognize the path from whence you came, to ride backward upon Yangqi’s three-legged donkey.
A single phrase of the head-word is like an iron stake; there is no need to bore into years of old paper.
Once all worldly possessions are cast away, one finally realizes that one has been deceived by the eyes all along.
A single phrase of the head-word is like an iron stake; you must know it the very moment the eyebrows move. The spirit of a patch-robed monk is naturally vast;
do not merely let the twelve hours of the day pass by in indolence.
Shishi’s Five-Leaf Attendant:
A single phrase of the hwadu is like an iron stake. There is no need to discuss the Three Mysteries or the Five Ranks; discard all the thousands of sutras and myriad classics.
Who is it that sweeps the floor and burns incense?
To the Chan practitioner Rongyu, I show that a single word-phrase is like an iron stake. Amidst the living, one requires a dead man. Meeting him, I report the news of my hometown:
purple stems and golden hips bloom amidst the dew.
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi, Volume Eighteen;
The Extensive Record of Chan Master Wuyi, Volume Nineteen.
Compiled by Honghan, Dharma Grandson residing at Boshan.

Verses of Instruction Collected by the Head Seat and Dharma Grandson Hongyu (5): To Layman Li Xuyun [Verse] The clouds of the mind are vast and boundless; The moon of wisdom shines clearly in the sky. When the wind of delusion ceases its blowing, The ocean of nature is calm and still. Do not seek outside yourself for the Way; Seek it within your own original face. If you can see this in an instant, You will transcend birth and death forever. [Verse] The Dharma is not something that can be grasped; It is like empty space, without form or trace. Do not mistake silence for the Way; Silence is merely the absence of speech. Do not mistake clarity for the Way; Clarity is merely the absence of darkness. Only when both speech and silence are transcended Will the true nature of reality be revealed. [Verse] The Great Matter is not far away; It lies right here before your eyes.
